api/Frontend.Runtime.Impl.GameImpl.Battl.title: Class RtsNetGameMode | Panzer War Document
api/Frontend.Runtime.Impl.GameImpl.Battl.summary: Class RtsNetGameMode Online RTS (BattleUnitOwnership.md §25, server docs/rts.md): every player picks a lineup within the budget per wave and deploys it whole; the server lays it out at one of their side's spawn points. Once all of a player's units are gone they wait out the cooldown and deploy again. Units are ordered from the map (the offline commander's RtsCommandController) or driven one at a time. The server owns the clock, the prices, the scores and the outcome. A unit's last order rides its sync state, so whoever simulates it next (the host for a player who left, the owner after a rejoin) carries it on. api/Frontend.Runtime.Impl.GameImpl.Battl.summary: Class WarZoneNetGameMode War zone network game mode: the capture zone map, except a sortie is bought rather than granted. Every price is the server's; this only shows the table it resolved. A room may let a player keep several vehicles (BattleUnitOwnership.md §16.3 A7): while alive they buy more at the usual price, each holding at its spawn point until driven. EventReference 结构，不是可拖放的 ScriptableObject。请在检视面板的事件选择器中挑选真实事件，例如 event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 [ { "tool": "list", "arguments": { "path": "static:FMODUnity.EventManager/Events", "fields": "Path,Guid/Data1,Guid/Data2,Guid/Data3,Guid/Data4", "search": "event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit", "count": 5 }, "expect": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)" }, "capture": { "Data1": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 1, "as": "int" }, "Data2": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 2, "as": "int" }, "Data3": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 3, "as": "int" }, "Data4": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 4, "as": "int" } } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:FMODUnity.EventManager/EventFromPath", "args": [ "event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "parameter:/engine01_cockpit/zoom" } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent", "values": { "eventReference": { "Path": "event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit", "Guid": { "Data1": "${Data1}", "Data2": "${Data2}", "Data3": "${Data3}", "Data4": "${Data4}" } } } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 3. 参数数组 展开 playParams 并添加一个元素，填写 key = zoom、value = 0.5。PlayParm 的两个字段分别为 string 和 float，组件在播放前逐个调用 setParameterByName。本配方会先查询当前事件缓存，确认示例事件存在并定义了 zoom；换用其他事件时，应填写该事件实际拥有的参数名。 每个要修改的参数各加一项。音效包需要加载时，组件会异步等待。实例准备好后，组件会在播放前写入各项参数。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent", "values": { "playParams": [ { "key": "zoom", "value": 0.5 } ] } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetComponent(ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent)/playParams/0/key" }, "expect": { "contains": "zoom" } } ] 4. 生命周期与距离 勾选 isCustomSoundMaxDistance，显示 customSoundMaxDistance 后填入 75；关闭覆盖时该字段隐藏。默认覆盖关闭、距离为 50。这里限制的是启用时是否开始播放，不是持续更新的声音衰减范围。 OnEnable 调用 Play。若此时相机距离超过上限，方法直接返回，靠近后不会自动重播；事件为空、音效池未准备好或音效包加载失败时也不会开始播放。禁用或销毁会取消尚未完成的等待：isStopEventOnDisable = true 时归还已有实例到池；设为 false 时走 ReleaseEvent 路径，不能据此保证声音立即停止。本例保持 true。 旧截图中的独立自动播放开关已移除。当前版本在对象启用时尝试播放。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent", "values": { "isStopEventOnDisable": true, "isCustomSoundMaxDistance": true, "customSoundMaxDistance": 75 } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetComponent(ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent)/customSoundMaxDistance" }, "expect": { "contains": "75" } } ] 配方验证了 prefab、事件引用和参数读回；实际音频输出、音效包加载和游戏内距离行为仍需运行时验证。

{ "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/editorAssetGuid", "value": "${editorGuid}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter/fireSpread/aimTime", "value": "2" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter/fireSpread/dispersion", "value": "0.35" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] } VehicleTextData 是载具配置的 ScriptableObject。本页只讲在 Unity Inspector vehicleTextData 引用。下文图片使用独立教学样例 Tutorial_VehicleTextData；在你的工程里请选择实际要制作的载具资产。 确认 AssetName 和 editorAssetGuid 属于目标载具；两者都是只读的资产标识字段，不能在此编辑。 editorAssetGuid 是 Unity 制作资产的 GUID，不是队列使用的 vehicleGuid。队列载具 ID 由 VehicleInfo.GetLoadGUID() 返回，两者含义不同，不要互相代填。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 CreateAsset 对应新建资产；inspect_set 的对象引用赋值对应拖放到引用槽。以下把新建的配置赋给独立的 VehicleData；只读字段仅查询。 [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateAsset", "args": [ "@static:UnityEngine.ScriptableObject/CreateInstance(ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleTextData)", "${fixture}/Tutorial_NewVehicleTextData.asset" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateAsset", "args": [ "@static:UnityEngine.ScriptableObject/CreateInstance(ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleData)", "${vehicleData}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicleData}/vehicleTextData", "value": "@asset:${asset}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "@asset:${asset}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/AssetName" }, "expect": { "contains": "TutorialTank" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/editorAssetGuid" }, "expect": { "contains": "${editorGuid}" } } ] 2. 设置生命值与视野 在 基础 分组下展开 基础数据（字段 PSParameter）。 在 摄像机控制 分组中找到 血量（PSParameter.Health，图中标记 1）。代码默认值为 1200，本例教学值也填 1200。 在 视野 分组中找到 观察范围（PSParameter.viewRange，图中标记 2）。允许范围是 220–5000，代码默认值为 220，本例教学值填 600。 保存资产，再重新选中该资产，确认 PSParameter.Health 与 PSParameter.viewRange 已写入目标资产，而不是其他资产。 PSParameter.Health=1200 和 PSParameter.viewRange=600 只是教学取值，不是官方平衡建议。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 路径使用真实代码字段名，不受编辑器语言影响。资产字段写入会保存；随后重新选择并读回断言。 [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/Health", "value": "1200" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/viewRange", "value": "600" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/SaveAssets", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "null" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "@asset:${asset}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/Health" }, "expect": { "contains": "1200" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/viewRange" }, "expect": { "contains": "600" } } ] 3. 高级参数 点击对应的 移动、开火、炮塔 或 多炮塔 标签页，再按下表寻找字段；杂项 位于标签页下方。 字段 Inspector 分组与含义 显示条件与读取行为 sharedGunData 共享主炮数据（开火） 始终显示；非空时 GetTankFireParam() 返回其中的 tankFireParameter。 TFParameter 主炮参数（开火） 仅当没有 sharedGunData 时显示；此时 GetTankFireParam() 返回它。 sharedTurretData 共享炮塔数据（炮塔） 始终显示；非空时 GetTurretParam() 返回其中的 turretParameter。 MTParameter 炮塔参数（炮塔） 仅当没有 sharedTurretData 时显示；此时 GetTurretParam() 返回它。 PTCParameter 履带参数（移动） 仅在 GetGroundType() 返回 TrackController（IsTrackController() 为真）时显示。 MechParameter 机甲参数（移动） 勾选 isMech 选择机甲控制器，可设置达到最大转向所需时间、步行特效和飞行参数。 CarControllerParameter 汽车参数（移动） 旧数据字段仍可见，当前的 GetGroundType() 不读取它。轮式载具使用车轮设置指南的现行路径。 MultiFireSystemData 旧版多炮塔系统（弃用） 旧版多炮塔列表，新载具不要新增。 simpleVehicleFireSystemParameters 新版多炮塔系统 当前多炮塔配置列表，元素类型为 SimpleVehicleFireSystemParameter。 vehicleSelfExplosionParams 自爆数据（杂项） 元素类型为 VehicleSelfExplosionTextParameter 的数组，按数组元素填写。 PTCParameter 的显示由 GetGroundType() 的判定顺序决定：isStationary → Stationary，MechParameter.isMech → MechController，LuaVehicleControllerParameter.isLua → Lua，ShipControllerParameter.isShip → Ship，其余情况才返回 TrackController。因此只把模型做成履带车，并不保证该字段出现。 sharedGunData 和 sharedTurretData 是共享引用：多个载具指向同一资产时，修改会影响所有引用者；没有共享引用时才分别使用 TFParameter 或 MTParameter。教学样例保留了 sharedGunData 引用，所以该样例中 TFParameter 不显示；这对只练习生命值与视野的步骤没有影响。 配置移动、开火、炮塔与自爆 履带车在 移动中设置动力、前进和倒车速度，绑定 TankWheelCollider 与 Track Data，再配置悬挂。车轮 · 履带悬挂 在 开火中选择炮弹、弹药容量、装填时间和开火音效。初速在所选炮弹资产中设置，主炮参数另有后坐比例与散布。当多辆车使用同一门炮时，可把这组参数放在共享主炮资产。 在 炮塔中设置回转范围、炮管升降速度、最大仰角和俯角。新副武器在 多炮塔页通过 simpleVehicleFireSystemParameters 设置节点和独立开火参数。维护旧载具时，参阅旧版多炮塔的模型路径和偏移。 配置游戏内自爆时，在 杂项的 vehicleSelfExplosionParams 增加一项，选择模型中的 explosionPath，再绑定 explosionParam.explosionData 对应的 SelfExplodeBullet。范围与伤害由该资源提供，触发方式由脚本决定。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 MCP 可按路径查询高级参数和显示条件，等价于定位数据。截图窗口目前不能自动选择 Odin 标签页；若新增教程需要标签页截图，应由 Codex 补该能力后再重拍。这里不改高级参数。 [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/sharedGunData" }, "expect": { "contains": "SharedGunData" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/noSharedGunData" }, "expect": { "contains": "False" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/noSharedTurretData" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetTankFireParam", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "TankFireParameter" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetTurretParam", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "TurretParameter" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetGroundType", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "TrackController" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PTCParameter" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/MultiFireSystemData" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/simpleVehicleFireSystemParameters" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/vehicleSelfExplosionParams" } }, { "expect": { "contains": "(Single)" }, "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/MechParameter/timeToFullyTurn" } }, { "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean)" }, "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/CarControllerParameter/isCar" } }, { "expect": { "regex": "Count=|\\(VehicleSelfExplosionTextParameter" }, "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/vehicleSelfExplosionParams" } } ] 4. 检查 确认 AssetName 和 editorAssetGuid 未变，PSParameter.Health 与 PSParameter.viewRange 已写入目标资产。 Inspector 截图只能证明字段位置与分组，不能证明运行时效果；要确认实际表现，需要在游戏内做一次检查。 如果后续需要调整高级参数，先确认上表的显示条件，再去对应分组里寻找字段。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 本配方验收资产绑定、标识和保存后的字段。教学样例没有完整可驾驶模型，未进行游戏内效果验证；截图成功不会记为运行时通过。 [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicleData}/vehicleTextData/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "Tutorial_VehicleTextData" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/AssetName" }, "expect": { "contains": "TutorialTank" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/editorAssetGuid" }, "expect": { "contains": "${editorGuid}" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/Health" }, "expect": { "contains": "1200" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/viewRange" }, "expect": { "contains": "600" } } ]

manual/en/component/fmod-play-component..title: Configure an FMOD Playback Component | Panzer War Document
manual/en/component/fmod-play-component..summary: Configure an FMOD Playback Component 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run fmod-play-component --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "asset": "${fixture}/Tutorial_Fmod.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } This page describes FmodPlayComponent: a MonoBehaviour that plays a configured FMOD event when its GameObject is enabled. 1. Component Add FmodPlayComponent to the GameObject that should emit sound. This example saves the component in a separate Tutorial_Fmod.prefab for reuse. Place that object at the required sound origin when using it in a scene. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "create", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent" } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 2. Event eventReference is a private [SerializeField] EventReference struct, not a draggable ScriptableObject. Choose a real event in the inspector event picker, for example event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "list", "arguments": { "path": "static:FMODUnity.EventManager/Events", "fields": "Path,Guid/Data1,Guid/Data2,Guid/Data3,Guid/Data4", "search": "event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit", "count": 5 }, "expect": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)" }, "capture": { "Data1": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 1, "as": "int" }, "Data2": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 2, "as": "int" }, "Data3": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 3, "as": "int" }, "Data4": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 4, "as": "int" } } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:FMODUnity.EventManager/EventFromPath", "args": [ "event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "parameter:/engine01_cockpit/zoom" } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent", "values": { "eventReference": { "Path": "event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit", "Guid": { "Data1": "${Data1}", "Data2": "${Data2}", "Data3": "${Data3}", "Data4": "${Data4}" } } } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 3. Parameters Expand playParams, add one entry and set key = zoom, value = 0.5. The PlayParm fields are a string and a float, passed to setParameterByName before playback. The recipe queries the current event cache to confirm that the example event exists and defines zoom. For another event, use its actual parameter names. Add one entry for each parameter you want to change. When the event's bank needs loading, the component waits for it asynchronously. Once an instance is ready, the component applies each configured parameter before starting playback. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent", "values": { "playParams": [ { "key": "zoom", "value": 0.5 } ] } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetComponent(ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent)/playParams/0/key" }, "expect": { "contains": "zoom" } } ] 4. Lifetime and distance Enable isCustomSoundMaxDistance, then set the revealed customSoundMaxDistance to 75. The field is hidden while the override is off. The defaults are false and 50. This is a check before starting playback, rather than a continuously updated attenuation range. OnEnable calls Play. If the camera is too far away at that point, playback does not start or automatically resume when it gets closer. An empty event, an unavailable pool or a failed bank load also prevents playback. Disabling or destroying the component cancels pending waits. With isStopEventOnDisable = true, an existing instance is returned to the pool; false takes the ReleaseEvent path and does not guarantee immediate silence. Keep it true for this example. The older Inspector showed a separate autoplay toggle. In the current component, enabling the GameObject starts the playback attempt. This page covers selecting the asset, locating fields, entering values and checking the result in the Unity Inspector. 1. Select the asset In the Project window, select the .asset whose main type is VehicleTextData. Its create menu is A Panzer War - 装甲纷争/G Ground Vehicle - 地面载具/Base - 载具配置/Vehicle Configuration - 载具配置参数. If you create a new asset, assign it to vehicleTextData on the target VehicleData. The pictures use a separate teaching sample named Tutorial_VehicleTextData; select the actual vehicle asset you are authoring in your project. Check that AssetName (shown as Default Asset Name. Do not modify it!) and editorAssetGuid (shown as Asset GUID) belong to the target vehicle. Both are read-only and cannot be edited here. editorAssetGuid is the Unity authoring-asset GUID, not the queue vehicleGuid. The queue vehicle ID comes from VehicleInfo.GetLoadGUID(). The two are different and must not be substituted for each other. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions CreateAsset is the asset-creation equivalent; assigning a live object with inspect_set is the reference-slot equivalent. The sample is assigned to a separate VehicleData. Read-only identifiers are queried only. Set HP and view range Expand PSParameter. It is under the Base BoxGroup and is labelled Player State Params. Inside PSParameter, find PSParameter.Health under the Camera Control group; it is labelled HP. The code default is 1200, and this example also uses the teaching value 1200. In the same PSParameter, find PSParameter.viewRange under the Sight group; it is labelled View Range. The allowed range is 220–5000, the code default is 220, and this example uses the teaching value 600. Save the asset, then reselect it and confirm HP and View Range were written to the target asset rather than another one. HP=1200 and viewRange=600 are teaching values only, not official balance guidance. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Paths use real code field names and remain stable across UI languages. Asset writes save the asset; reselect and read back the values to verify. [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/Health", "value": "1200" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/viewRange", "value": "600" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/SaveAssets", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "null" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "@asset:${asset}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/Health" }, "expect": { "contains": "1200" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/viewRange" }, "expect": { "contains": "600" } } ] 3. Advanced groups Select the relevant Mobility, Fire, Turret or Multi-Turret tab before locating a field below. The Misc group is below the tabs. Field Inspector group and label Visibility and read behavior sharedGunData Shared Gun Data (Fire) Always shown; when set, GetTankFireParam() returns its tankFireParameter. TFParameter Tank Fire Params (Fire) Shown only when sharedGunData is empty; GetTankFireParam() then returns it. sharedTurretData Shared Turret Data (Turret) Always shown; when set, GetTurretParam() returns its turretParameter. MTParameter Turret Params (Turret) Shown only when sharedTurretData is empty; GetTurretParam() then returns it. PTCParameter Track Params (Mobility) Shown only when GetGroundType() returns TrackController, i.e. IsTrackController() is true. MechParameter Mech Params (Mobility) Enable isMech for the mech controller. Configure turn response, walking effects, and flight. CarControllerParameter Car Params (Mobility) Older data still appears here. The current GetGroundType() ignores this field. Follow the wheel setup guide for a wheeled vehicle. MultiFireSystemData Old Multi-Turret (Deprecated) Legacy multi-turret list; do not add it to new vehicles. simpleVehicleFireSystemParameters New Multi-Turret Current multi-turret list; each element is a SimpleVehicleFireSystemParameter. vehicleSelfExplosionParams Self Explosion Params (Misc) An array of VehicleSelfExplosionTextParameter; fill it element by element. PTCParameter visibility follows the order inside GetGroundType(): isStationary → Stationary, MechParameter.isMech → MechController, LuaVehicleControllerParameter.isLua → Lua, ShipControllerParameter.isShip → Ship, and only the remaining case returns TrackController. A tracked model does not by itself guarantee the field. sharedGunData and sharedTurretData are shared references: when several vehicles point to the same asset, edits affect every referencing vehicle; use TFParameter or MTParameter only when no shared reference is assigned. The teaching sample keeps a sharedGunData reference, so TFParameter is hidden there; this does not affect the HP and View Range steps above. Configure movement, firing, the turret, and self-destruction For tracks, configure power and forward and reverse speed under Mobility. Assign TankWheelCollider and Track Data before setting up the suspension. Wheels · Track suspension Under Fire, choose the shells, ammo capacity, reload time, and firing sound. Set muzzle velocity on the selected shell asset. The gun parameters control recoil scale and dispersion. Use a shared gun asset when several vehicles need the same gun settings. Under Turret, set the traverse range, barrel elevation speed, and maximum elevation and depression. For a new secondary weapon, use simpleVehicleFireSystemParameters in the multi-turret tab to bind model nodes and independent firing data. For existing vehicles, see the legacy paths and offsets. To configure an in-game self-destruct effect, add an entry under vehicleSelfExplosionParams in the miscellaneous settings. Assign the model's explosionPath and put a SelfExplodeBullet in explosionParam.explosionData. The asset provides range and damage, and the script determines when the effect fires. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions MCP paths locate advanced data and visibility conditions directly. The capture window cannot yet select Odin tabs automatically; Codex must add that capability before a tutorial needs such a capture. This group does not alter advanced settings. To create a map for the current game, use the Map Workshop. Before distributing a Ravenfield map, make sure you have permission to publish it and its assets. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Core.RvlResourceManager/IsSupport" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) False" } } ] View the legacy Steam map and configuration format Use these steps to identify old files or recover settings from a legacy archive. The former Steam Free edition supported the Maps - Mod Tools category of the Ravenfield Workshop. Subscribed items were downloaded to the Steam library under steamapps/workshop/content/636480, in a subfolder for each item. Legacy Ravenfield Workshop category Locate the file ending in .rfl. Installations that supported this format used steamapps/common/PanzerWar-DE/dlc/PanzerWar/Mods/StandaloneWindows64_RvlMaps. When a compatible client started, it generated map-name.rfl.yaml next to the map. To correct misplaced spawn points, set isCustomPoints: true and update the coordinates for both teams. Add one x, y, and z block per point. This example retains the original field names and capitalization. isCustomPoints: true customTeamASpawnPoints: - x: 0 y: 0 z: 0 - x: -4 y: 0 z: -4 - x: 4 y: 0 z: 4 customTeamBSpawnPoints: - x: 0 y: 0 z: 0 customPartolPoints: - x: 0 y: 0 z: 0 tileSize: 512 voxelSize: 2 The original sharing workflow put the .rfl and its YAML in a ZIP named StandaloneWindows64_Example.modpack. Some old maps may fail to load or crash a legacy client.

manual/en/mod/blender-axis-fix.html.summary: Correct model axes in Blender 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run blender-axis-fix Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "asset": "${fixture}/Tutorial_AxisCheck.fbx" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } Use these steps when a model needs a different local rotation basis. Work on a copy. 1. Adjust the rotation and export Select the affected object in Unity's Scene view. Set the tool orientation to Local and the handle position to Pivot. Record a known hull dimension and check whether Z points forward and Y points up. Work on a copy in Blender Object Mode. Select the object whose local rotation basis needs fixing. Press R, X, -90, then Enter. Press Ctrl+A and choose Rotation. Check that the rotation values read zero after applying it. Press R, X, 90, then Enter. Choose File → Export → FBX. Use Scale 1.00, Apply Scalings → FBX Units Scale, Forward → −Z Forward, and Up → Y Up. Import the FBX into a test folder in Unity. The Blender script regenerates the teaching example. The Unity MCP recipe below imports the resulting sample FBX. blender --background --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 --python Tools/ManualMcp/BlenderAxisFix/build_model.py -- Tutorial_AxisCheck.fbx Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/Editor/DocumentationSamples/blender-axis-fix/Tutorial_AxisCheck.fbx", "${asset}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/ImportAsset", "args": [ "${asset}", "ForceSynchronousImport" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 2. Check the model's forward and up directions In Unity, verify that the front points along +Z and the top along +Y. Compare the dimensions with the original hull, then rotate the turret and gun separately on the copy to verify their pivots. The sample puts NoseMarker at (0, 0, 1) and RoofMarker at (0, 1, 0). manual/en/mod/capture-mode-config.html.title: Capture mode config | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/capture-mode-config.html.summary: Capture mode config 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run capture-mode-config A capture zone mode config describes the zones, capture points, per-zone spawns and zone connectivity used by a capture-zone battle. It is a CaptureZoneModeConfig JSON stored under the config root and packed into binary config data at build time. 1. Prepare the map scene Complete Set the Steam game folder so the Editor can read the game's LuaProject assets. For a DIY map, follow Import a DIY map into the Unity project and load the YAML into the base playground. For an official or other non-DIY map, just open the desired scene in the Editor. Keep the scene open while editing. Point placement and the Refresh Position (NavMesh) button sample the NavMesh of the open scene, so the map must already have its NavMesh in place. 2. Create the config Open Framework - 框架 → 2. Config - 配置文件. In the creation form, choose Config Path. The dropdown lists the config paths stored in the framework settings; the value also decides which folder tree the config appears in. Choose the serialized config type CaptureZoneModeConfig. Enter a File Name and click Create Config. An empty file name only shows an error dialog, so fill it first. The file name does not need an extension. The tool writes <config root>/CaptureZone/<name>.json and assigns a fresh GUID internally. Do not copy GUIDs from another file. The created object has these fields, and they serve different purposes: Field Purpose captureZoneName Internal identifier. Use a distinct, unique ID; do not reuse one across configs. displayName User-facing localized name shown to players. mapGuid Runtime map identifier. Use the MapData GUID for regular maps and the Defined Name for DIY maps. backgroundCameraTransformInfo Optional camera position and rotation for the map background view. The Editor menu tree lists the file as <config path folder>/CaptureZone/<file name>, and selecting it opens the capture zone editor for that file. 3. Set the map GUID and background camera In the zone editor, the Map Guid row shows the current value (empty shows —). Click Use Current Scene to fill it from the map data that is discoverable for the active scene. For a regular map, check the saved value against the GUID in MapData. For a DIY map, enter the exact Defined Name (definedName) from the imported YAML, including spaces and punctuation. The game registers the DIY map under that name. The background camera is optional. Click Set Bg Camera while the Scene view is framed the way you want, and it stores that camera position and rotation. Leave it at zero if the mode does not need a background camera. 4. Add capture zones Click + New Zone in the editor panel or the scene overlay. The zone is added at the current scene view point with a placeholder pointName (Zone_<n>) and a default radius of 30. Click the zone label to select it, then fill in: pointName — must be unique. Zone chains resolve zones by this string, so renaming a zone means updating the chains too. Position and Radius — the capture point and capture circle. Default Owner — initial team owner, or none for neutral. Build the perimeter with +Pt / -Pt on the selected zone. zonePoints is the perimeter polygon that defines the zone area; it is separate from the capture point position and radius. Place perimeter points on walkable ground and use Refresh Position (NavMesh) and Merge Nearby Points to snap and tidy them. Repeat for every zone. A small map usually needs 2-3 zones; do not invent extra zones just to fill the array. 5. Add per-zone spawns Select the zone and click Show Spawn (older builds labelled it Edit), then + to add a spawn marker. A numbered marker appears. Click it to select that spawn and move or rotate it with the scene handles. The values are saved in the zone's spawnTransformInfos and can also be edited in the serialized fields. Choose clear drivable poses: on or next to the ground, facing the intended direction, and not inside walls, props or other vehicles. Refresh Position (NavMesh) snaps spawn positions to the navmesh and zeroes pitch and roll, which helps but still needs a visual check. Click Hide Spawn when done to declutter the scene view. 6. Add zone chains Add entries to zoneChains, using A and B with the same pointName strings that exist on the zones. Connect only the neighbours that the map design intends to be connected. The runtime CaptureZoneGameMode.Setup.cs reads fromZone as a prerequisite neighbour for toZone, so each entry is directional. Add both directions only when the map design really allows travel both ways. Check every link: names must resolve to existing zones. Unresolved names are silently skipped at runtime and are not drawn by the editor, so a typo simply removes the connection. 7. Save, pack and test Save the config. Add the saved capture-zone JSON to Config file in the map mod's build pipeline. Select the target platform and build the mod package. The pipeline converts the JSON into configuration data and includes it in the .modpack. Use the map build workflow for the scene itself. For a local export of the configuration data, click Pack All Configs. This rebuilds Build/Config and writes the capture-zone data to Build/Config/capturezone/<config GUID>.bytes. Install the built mod and start a capture battle on the target map. Check the zones, their spawn points, and the order in which the teams can advance. The example checks the configuration for Tutorial Town with two regions, Depot and Ridge. The chain in the example permits progression from Depot to Ridge. It writes and verifies a local .bytes file. manual/en/mod/custom-shader-data.html.summary: Custom Shader Data for Vehicles 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run custom-shader-data --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "package": "${fixture}/Docs_${runId}_Package.asset", "pipeline": "${fixture}/Docs_${runId}_Pipeline.asset", "shaderData": "${fixture}/Tutorial_CustomShader.asset", "packageGuid": "4ccfd3f8-eabc-44d6-b599-82486dbd4604" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "@static:UnityEngine.ScriptableObject/CreateInstance(ShanghaiWindy.Core.ModPackageBuildPiplineData)", "${pipeline}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" }, "phase": "build" }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${package}/localizedModName/defaultName", "value": "Tutorial Package" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" }, "phase": "build" }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${package}/localizedDescription/defaultName", "value": "Documentation teaching package" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" }, "phase": "build" }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${package}/author", "value": "Documentation" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" }, "phase": "build" }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${package}/supportURL", "value": "https://doc.game.windyverse.net/" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" }, "phase": "build" }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${package}/guid", "value": "${packageGuid}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" }, "phase": "build" }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${pipeline}/linkedModPackage", "value": "@asset:${package}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" }, "phase": "build" } ] } Use this tutorial when a vehicle needs a shader and material that the built-in shader types do not provide. A CustomShaderData asset stores the custom Material plus channel-name mappings, and CoreRPMatComponent selects it per renderer material slot at runtime. A custom shader is a Unity shader project of its own. If the Unity Material, Shader Graph or URP/HDRP basics are new to you, read those first; this page only covers how Panzer War plugs your material into a vehicle. 1. Prepare the materials Build and test the Shader Graph / shader in the target render pipeline (URP or HDRP), not in the other one. Create one Material per pipeline that uses that shader. The URP material and the HDRP material are separate assets with separate pipeline requirements; a material packed for HDRP cannot serve URP. Keep the source vehicle textures (albedo, normal, mask) and base colour out of the custom shader defaults. The game writes them back at runtime under the channel names you configure, so the shader must expose those names. 2. Create the Custom Shader Data In the Project window choose Create > A Panzer War - 装甲纷争 > C Config - 配置 > Custom Material - 自定义材质 to create a CustomShaderData asset. The inspector of that asset (CustomShaderDataEditor) fills guid automatically when the asset is opened, and provides: 复制唯一标识 - Copy Guid: copies the generated guid to the clipboard. This is the identifier you paste into the component later. 创建新的唯一标识 - Create new guid: clears the guid and lets it regenerate. Every reference to the old guid breaks, so only do this before the data is referenced by vehicles or another mod. Assign your tested Material to Custom Material (overrideMaterialPath) by picking it from the material dropdown. This is the material whose properties are copied onto the vehicle material. Default vs Custom Vehicle Option customShaderType has two values: 默认 - Default (Default) shows overrideMaterialPath and customKeywords. The loader can still fill the vehicle's texture and color inputs through the default channel names. 自定义载具选项 - Custom Vehicle Option (VehicleOption): additionally shows the channel names the game uses when it restores the vehicle's own maps and colour: Field Meaning Default customMainTexName Channel the vehicle albedo map is written to _BaseMap customNormalTexName Channel the vehicle normal map is written to _BumpMap customMaskTexName Channel the vehicle mask map is written to _MaskMap customBaseColor Channel the vehicle base colour is written to _BaseColor Change these only when your shader uses different property names. The names must match the shader exactly, including case. 3. Configure CoreRPMatComponent Add CoreRPMatComponent to the object that owns the MeshRenderer you want to re-shade. Enable Component Based (isComponentBased). Add one entry to indexCoreRPMatParams per material slot you want to override. index is the material slot number on that Mesh Renderer, starting at 0. In each entry set Shader (coreRPShaderType) to Custom. This reveals customNatParam. Fill customNatParam: urpMaterialGuid: the guid of the CustomShaderData whose Material targets URP. hdrpMaterialGuid: the guid of the CustomShaderData whose Material targets HDRP. The two GUIDs must be different, and each must point to material data built for the matching pipeline. Do not put a URP GUID into hdrpMaterialGuid. The GUID is resolved when the vehicle's resources load. An empty GUID uses the renderer's default shader. When a nonempty GUID fails to resolve or its material bundle is absent, the loader logs the fallback. Supply valid data for each pipeline where the vehicle should use the custom shader. customNatParam also carries per-slot channel writes: customTextureChannels: channelName plus channelTex, written directly to the material. customColorChannel: channelName plus either a normal colour or, with isHDR enabled, an HDR colour. These are useful for per-vehicle variations (markings, lamp colours, insignia) that should not live in the shared custom material. 4. Package it Single vehicle: keep the CustomShaderData asset in the same mod package as that vehicle's VehicleInfo and other vehicle resources, and build them together. Shared across vehicles or mods: build the CustomShaderData (and its materials) as its own mod package, and have the vehicle mod declare an explicit dependency on that package by its package GUID. Do not rely on load order or on the asset merely existing in another package. The shipped guid is part of the runtime contract. Rebuilding a shared shader mod with new GUIDs silently breaks every dependant, so treat GUIDs as stable once published. 5. What happens at runtime For a renderer whose slot resolves to Custom, the shader asset manager: Resolves the CustomShaderData by the pipeline-specific GUID (urpMaterialGuid or hdrpMaterialGuid). Loads the custom material, assigns its shader to the vehicle material, and copies the custom material's properties (including toggles and dropdown values) onto it. Restores the vehicle's own data: albedo, normal and mask maps plus base colour are written to customMainTexName, customNormalTexName, customMaskTexName and customBaseColor. Enables the keywords listed in customKeywords whose isTextureChannelCondition condition is satisfied (that is, the referenced texture channel is assigned), and writes the per-slot texture and colour channels. Property copying happens before the vehicle data is restored, so anything your custom material sets on the four mapped channels is overwritten by the vehicle's own textures and colour. Use other property names for values that must survive. Not every property you author is guaranteed to survive: copying is generic (name-based), while the vehicle maps and base colour are restored explicitly. Verify the properties you depend on in the actual game build. 6. Optional channel conventions The vehicle camouflage and dirt systems use a set of conventional names. They are optional: use them only if your shader implements the matching behaviour. They are shader-side conventions, not properties the loader guarantees to populate. Channel name Type Convention _Smoothness float Smoothness _CamoPatternMap Texture2D Camouflage pattern map _CamoPatternTiling Vector4 Tiling of the pattern map _CamoBlackTint Color Colour mixed for the pattern map's black channel _CamoRedTint Color Colour mixed for the pattern map's red channel _CamoGreenTint Color Colour mixed for the pattern map's green channel _CamoBlueTint Color Colour mixed for the pattern map's blue channel _Lerp float (0-1) Blend weight of the camouflage colour _DirtTex Texture2D Dirt texture _DirtRange float (0-1) Dirt blend weight _KEYWORD_ENABLE_CAMO keyword Camouflage enabled (used by VehicleCamoManager) _KEYWORD_ENABLE_CAMO_COLOR_TEX keyword Texture-based camouflage enabled _KEYWORDENABLEDIRT keyword Dirt texture enabled Notes: _KEYWORD_ENABLE_CAMO and _KEYWORD_ENABLE_CAMO_COLOR_TEX are the keywords the current VehicleCamoManager drives. The older _EnableCamo / _EnableCamoColorTex property names you may see in old shaders are not the same thing. _KEYWORDENABLEDIRT is the dirt keyword name. The blending described below is the legacy sample shader graph behaviour, shown as an example of how the channels can be combined, not a rule the loader enforces. A custom shader that ignores dirt channels simply renders without dirt. Example dirt behaviour from the legacy sample: when _KEYWORDENABLEDIRT is enabled, the vehicle AO map is blended with _DirtTex at the strength given by _DirtRange. Reimplement it in your graph if you want that look. 7. RGBA pattern and tint technique The camouflage pattern technique used by the sample shaders: treat _CamoPatternMap as four independent masks, split the RGBA channels, and lerp each channel's tint colour (_CamoBlackTint, _CamoRedTint, _CamoGreenTint, _CamoBlueTint) into the base colour using that channel as the mask, then blend the whole result with the base colour by _Lerp (clamped to 0-1). Gate the branch with _KEYWORD_ENABLE_CAMO / _KEYWORD_ENABLE_CAMO_COLOR_TEX so vehicles without camouflage keep their plain look. The same idea works for any per-vehicle data: a mask texture plus tint colours gives you markings, stencils or wear patterns without shipping a separate material per vehicle. 8. Shader authoring notes The asset inspector recommends multi_compile for your keywords. If you use shader_feature, build with the shader variant collection so variants are not stripped and the keyword silently stops working in player builds. Declare every keyword you toggle from customKeywords in the shader, and keep the keyword string identical to the field in the asset. Avoid shader_feature variants that only exist in the editor; check the player build, not just Play Mode. 9. Verify in the target renderer Open the vehicle in the URP project and confirm the custom look appears; then repeat in the HDRP project with the HDRP GUID and material. Each pipeline must be checked separately. Confirm the vehicle's own albedo, normal, mask and base colour reach the intended channels by temporarily tinting the base colour or swapping a texture. Toggle a camouflage or dirt option and confirm the keyword actually changes the result in a build, not only in the editor. Load a second vehicle that shares the custom shader mod to confirm the shared package dependency resolves. Check the log for loader errors about unresolved GUIDs or missing material bundles; those indicate a wrong GUID, a pipeline mismatch, or a package that was not built with the asset. The MCP example builds a Windows package from a teaching material and its data asset. Check the final appearance in the target renderer using the steps above. manual/en/mod/destructible-object-creati.title: Create a destructible object with shattered prefabs | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/destructible-object-creati.summary: Create a destructible object with shattered prefabs 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run destructible-object-creation --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "intact": "${fixture}/Tutorial_Fence_Intact.prefab", "fractured": "${fixture}/Tutorial_Fence_Fractured.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } This workflow uses RayFire Shatter to cut an intact model into fragments, then turns those fragments into a prefab driven by RayFire Rigid. It suits props such as fences and walls that should break apart as a whole. If you only need to swap between an intact and a damaged model, see destructible objects: model replacement. Prepare the model and the Shatter component Place the intact model in the scene and select the object that has the mesh. Search Add Component for Rayfire Shatter. If you started with a prefab, fragment its scene instance and save the resulting fragments to a new prefab. Set fragment parameters and split In the component's Fragments section, choose the fragment type; the sample uses Type=Voronoi and Amount=3. Inner Surface Material is configurable and controls how the broken faces look; the sample value is only a reference. Once the parameters look right, click the Fragment button to split the object. Export the fragment mesh In the Export section, set Source to Last Fragments, set Suffix to _frags, then click Export Last Fragments to save the cut mesh. Organize the hierarchy and save a prefab Select the new *_root object after splitting. The original fence example used Prop_Fence_01B_root, with children named like *_sh_#. Expand the root to check its fragments and mesh references, then drag it into Project as a prefab. Keep the exported mesh asset because the prefab references its fragment meshes. Attach Rayfire Rigid to the root of the saved prefab. Configure RayFire Rigid On RayFire Rigid, set Object Type to Mesh Root, then click Editor Setup so the component registers the fragments from the current hierarchy. The sample also uses Initialization=By Method, Simulation Type=Dynamic, material Concrete, and a Mesh collider. Adjust these to the prop's actual material and how it should react. Assign the Fracture Layer Select the fragment children under the generated root in Hierarchy and set their Layer to Fracture. Save and reopen the prefab to check the layer and exported mesh references. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Fragment a teaching prop in an isolated scene with RayFire, export the mesh, and save a Mesh Root prefab with Fracture children. [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Core.AssetBundleManager/LuaEnv/DoString", "args": [ "local run = assert(loadfile(\"../../Docs/Manual/tutorials/destructible-object-creation/example.lua\"))()\nreturn run(\"${fixture}\")", "docs-rayfire", "null" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "RayFire saved 3 mesh fragments with Mesh Root and Fracture layer" } } ] Test Place the prefab in an isolated test scene and trigger the destruction. Check that the fragments separate as expected, the inner surface material is correct, and the fragment layer applies. An isolated scene keeps other map objects from confusing the result. The saved mesh and prefab should match the description above; if the fragment count or names differ, regenerate them from the export step. For the model replacement route, see destructible objects.

Import a DIY map into the Unity project 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run diy-map-project-import 1. Prepare the assets and the YAML file Open the public SDK's UnityProject using project setup. Maintainers with access to official production assets use Panzer-War-Mods/Projects/Maps. Map asset sources A DIY save finds objects by itemGuid. The official Maps project already declares the DIY packages in its manifest. For the public SDK, if you have the corresponding local UPM packages, use Window → Package Manager → + → Add package from disk and select each package.json. Check that their assets and configuration appear under Packages in Project. Find the .yaml in the game's save directory and make a copy for editing. The source assets need the same GUIDs used by the save. 2. Load the base scene and import the map Open Framework → 1. Editor Tools → 05. DIY Workshop → DIY Map Edit. Choose Load Base Asset and confirm to enter Play in the base playground. Wait for the game environment to finish loading. Select the file in the YAML picker, then click Load DIY Map from Yaml. Inspect the scene and DIYMapConfig after the import finishes. If an object is missing, find the reported itemGuid in the Console. Check that the package containing that GUID is available before continuing. Keep existing GUIDs so saves can resolve their objects. manual/en/mod/editor-configs.html.title: Custom internal module presets | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/editor-configs.html.summary:
Custom internal module presets 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run editor-configs The module preset list in the damage model editor comes from two built-in folders and one local configuration array. Lay out the models and register your root folder in the order below to pick your own internal modules from the editor. 1. Create the module folders Create a root folder and module type subfolders in the SDK project, then put the models directly in the subfolders: Assets/MyModulePresets/ Engine/ EngineA.fbx Crew/ CrewA.fbx The current scanner reads only direct *.fbx and *.prefab files under <root>/<type> and does not recurse into subfolders. A type folder name must be the EInternalModuleType member name, case-sensitive, such as Engine, Crew, AmmoShell, Breech, or Transmission. It is not the displayed caption or a string like E 引擎 (Engine). Folder name Module Transmission Transmission Engine Engine HeatSink Heat sink OilTank Oil tank Traversing Traversing gear Breech Breech Elevator Elevator Sighting Sighting AmmoShell Ammo rack Crew Crew InternalArmor Internal armor Radiator Radar (Inspector: Radiator) AutoReloader Auto reloader OilPipline Oil pipeline SurfaceControlRope Surface control rope 2. Prepare the models The model root needs a usable MeshFilter and shared mesh. When a preset is picked, if the model has no collider, ModulePresetUtil.SetupModule adds a MeshCollider that references that shared mesh, plus a kinematic rigidbody. An empty mesh cannot produce the collider. You can also ship modules as prefabs, placed as .prefab in the same type folder. The file name is only used for display and does not affect the category. 3. Register the root folder in the local config Open Framework → 1. Editor Tools and find Editor Config under 01. ♥ Core Tools. Add Assets/MyModulePresets to Module Preset Folder. Enter the root folder. Click Save to write the current Unity project's Assets/EditorStorage.json. To edit the file offline, close Unity, then back it up. In the public SDK, the path is UnityProject/Assets/EditorStorage.json. Keep the other keys and add the root to the existing modulePresetFolders array: { "modulePresetFolders": [ "Assets/MyModulePresets" ] } Write only the root folder. Do not append /Engine and do not add a trailing slash. Keep the other keys in the file; do not replace an existing config with a minimal object. If the local Assets/EditorStorage.json file does not exist yet, save once from Editor Config. Do not edit this file while Unity is open: EditorStorage.Save writes the whole in-memory object back, so stale values can overwrite your edit. 4. Use the preset in the damage model editor Open the target vehicle with the 伤害模型编辑器 - HitBox Editor (VehicleHitBoxEditorWindow) and enter prefab edit mode for that damage model prefab. Outside prefab mode the window only shows a hint. Press 刷新预设 - Refresh so the scan re-reads the folders. Pick the target type in 选择的模块类型 - Pick Module Type. Find its thumbnail. Clicking the thumbnail only pings the asset; the 选择 - Pick button below it instantiates the module into the current prefab. Adjust position and size, then press Ctrl + S to save the prefab. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Add a temporary preset root, verify scanning of a direct prefab and initialize a Breech component. The replay restores the in-memory settings. [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Core.AssetBundleManager/LuaEnv/DoString", "args": [ "local u, e = CS.UnityEngine, CS.UnityEditor
local database = e.AssetDatabase
local scratch = "Assets/__DocsPresetScan"
assert(not database.IsValidFolder(scratch), "Scratch folder already exists")
local presets = CS.ShanghaiWindy.Editor.EditorStorage.Info.modulePresetFolders
local moduleType = CS.ShanghaiWindy.Core.EInternalModuleType
local block
local added = false
local ok, result = pcall(function()
 database.CreateFolder("Assets", "__DocsPresetScan")
 database.CreateFolder(scratch, "Breech")
 database.CreateFolder(scratch .. "/Breech", "Nested")
 block = u.GameObject.CreatePrimitive(u.PrimitiveType.Cube)
 u.Object.DestroyImmediate(block:GetComponent(typeof(u.Collider)))
 local path = scratch .. "/Breech/Sample.prefab"
 assert(e.PrefabUtility.SaveAsPrefabAsset(block, path))
 assert(e.PrefabUtility.SaveAsPrefabAsset(block, scratch .. "/Breech/Nested/Hidden.prefab"))
 presets:Add(scratch)
 added = true
 local mapping = CS.System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary(CS.System.String, moduleType)()
 local util = CS.ShanghaiWindy.Editor.ModulePresetUtil
 util.RefreshModuleMapping(mapping)
 assert(mapping:ContainsKey(path), "Direct prefab was not scanned")
 local entries = mapping:GetEnumerator()
 local found
 while entries:MoveNext() do
 if entries.Current.Key == path then found = entries.Current.Value end
 end
 assert(found and found:ToString() == "Breech", "Wrong scanned type: " .. tostring(found))
 assert(not mapping:ContainsKey(scratch .. "/Breech/Nested/Hidden.prefab"), "Nested prefab was scanned")
 local module = util.SetupModule(block, moduleType.Breech)
 assert(module.moduleType:ToString() == "Breech", "Wrong placed module type: " .. tostring(module.moduleType))
end)
if added then presets:RemoveAt(presets.Count - 1) end
if block then u.Object.DestroyImmediate(block) end
if database.IsValidFolder(scratch) then database.DeleteAsset(scratch) end
assert(ok, result)
return "Module prefab preset scan and placement passed"", "manual-preset", "null" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "Module prefab preset scan and placement passed" } } ] 5. Troubleshooting Symptom Check Custom models are not listed Whether the root is in the array; whether the type folder matches the enum name exactly; whether the file is a direct .fbx or .prefab in that folder; whether you refreshed after the change Thumbnail appears but the picked module has no collider Whether the model root has a MeshFilter with a valid shared mesh An old model still shows after replacing files Refresh presets, then pick again; confirm the file is not in a subfolder Wrong category The file's type folder does not match an EInternalModuleType member Built-in example folders The current code also scans Assets/Res/InternalDamage/Preset/<type> and Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.middlesharedresources/SharedInternalDamage/Preset/<type> (package constant PackageConst.MIDDLE_SHARED_RESOURCES). Use their files as examples of naming and structure. The middle shared resources package is a dependency package and its sources are not necessarily present in the local Packages folder. Related sources: ModulePresetUtil.RefreshModuleMapping, ModulePresetUtil.AddModule, ModulePresetUtil.SetupModule, ModulePresetUtil.DrawModulePreset, EditorStorageInfo.modulePresetFolders, VehicleHitBoxEditorWindow.RefreshPresets, EInternalModuleType.

manual/en/mod/fixed-angle-reload.html.summary: Fixed-Angle Reload Configuration 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run fixed-angle-reload --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "sharedGun": "${fixture}/Tutorial_FixedAngleReload_SharedGunData.asset", "vehicle": "${fixture}/Tutorial_FixedAngleReload_VehicleTextData.asset" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/PatriotRadar/BuiltIn-Patriot-Radar-SharedGun.asset", "${sharedGun}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/PatriotRadar/BuiltIn-Patriot-Radar_VehicleTextData.asset", "${vehicle}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } } ] } Fixed-angle reload uses the gun buff TankFireSpecificAngleReloadBuff. After firing or switching shell type, it can wait for a configured delay, constrain turret angles and scale rotation speeds. The constraint is removed after reloading finishes. 1. Prepare shared gun parameters In the Project window choose Create > A Panzer War - 装甲纷争 > G Ground Vehicle - 地面载具 > Shared Data - 共享数据 > Gun - 炮管 to create SharedGunData. Expand tankFireParameter and find the Buffs reference list, buffRefs. This recipe copies an existing gun configuration to preserve its initialization data. Editing shared gun data affects all referencing vehicles. For a change to one vehicle, create a separate shared-data copy, or clear that vehicle's sharedGunData before editing its own TFParameter. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "@asset:${sharedGun}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter" }, "expect": { "contains": "TankFireParameter" } } ] 2. Add the fixed-angle reload buff In the main gun's Tank Fire Params → Misc Settings → Buffs (buffRefs), click +. Open the entry's Value type menu and pick TankFireSpecificAngleReloadBuff. Expand it and enter the sample values: Field Teaching value and meaning hasDelay / delay Enable the delay and set it to 0.5 seconds isTraverseLocked Enable Lock Traverse hasSpecificTraverseAngle / specificTraverseAngle Enable the specific traverse angle and set 0 degrees hasSpecificElevationAngle / specificElevationAngle Enable the specific elevation angle and set 5 degrees isOverrideTraverseSpeed / overrideTraverseSpeedCoff Override traverse speed with -0.5, a 50% reduction isOverrideElevationSpeed Leave disabled to preserve elevation speed Each switch controls its corresponding field. With traverse locked, the turret holds the configured angle or the angle at the start of the reload state. With traverse unlocked, the turret continues following the aim point. Elevation independently holds its configured angle or its angle on entry. Click Save on the reference entry, then save the gun asset. The current list is AbstractTankFireBuffCasterSafeRef[]; the legacy buffs field is deprecated. The MCP recipe creates a real SafeRef entry by supplying both its type and configuration JSON. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Whole-array JSON assignment creates real SafeRef entries with the type name and serialized configuration. The recipe verifies persisted data and leaves deprecated buffs untouched. Bind it to a vehicle Assign the shared gun asset to VehicleTextData.sharedGunData. When set, GetTankFireParam() reads that asset's tankFireParameter. Without a shared reference, it reads the vehicle's TFParameter. Save and read the buff configuration back to confirm the intended asset is used. manual/en/mod/fmod-profiler.html.title: Record audio events with FMOD Profiler | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/fmod-profiler.html.summary: Record audio events with FMOD Profiler 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run fmod-profiler Profiler records audio events, levels, CPU usage, and memory. Set up the FMOD project and banks and load a Unity scene that can play the sound you want to diagnose. 1. Enable the live connection In Unity, open FMOD → Edit Settings and select the platform you are testing. Use Play in Editor in the Editor or the target platform for a standalone build. Enable Live Update and read the Live Update Port. FMOD defaults to 9264. The Editor configuration used here reported 9000. Connect to the port shown for your platform. Rebuild a standalone player after changing its setting. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "static:FMODUnity.Settings/Instance/PlayInEditorPlatform/IsLiveUpdateEnabled" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean)" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "static:FMODUnity.Settings/Instance/PlayInEditorPlatform/LiveUpdatePort" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Int32)" } } ] In FMOD Studio, open the project that generated those banks. Enter Play Mode in Unity or start your test build. In Studio, choose File → Connect to Game. On the same computer, enter localhost:<port>, such as localhost:9000. For a separate test device, enter its reachable address and port. A green Live Update ON in the lower-right corner confirms the connection. FMOD Live Update 2. Record and diagnose levels Open Window → Profiler in Studio and click the round Record button. Reproduce the issue once in Unity, then click Stop. Locate the test on the timeline. Select the event track in the left pane, look at the event instances and levels for that period, and compare them with Mixer CPU and memory usage. Open Window → Mixer and follow the event's output through its buses to the master. Listen to the running game and compare it with a Studio audition or an earlier reference recording. If timing looks correct but levels sound wrong, check the source audio, event and bus gains, and Unity volume settings separately. Save the session, change one setting, and record a second pass for comparison. Profiler can also record an audition directly in Studio. FMOD Profiler manual The MCP actions above read the connection settings for the Unity platform. Connect and record in FMOD Studio.

manual/en/mod/get-started.html.title: Set up the mod project | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/get-started.html.summary: Set up the mod project 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run get-started Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "sdkCheckout": "../../../Panzer-War-Mod-SDK" }, "calls": [] } 1. Download and extract the SDK Open the Panzer War Mod SDK release page and expand Assets. Download the release ZIP named Panzer-War-Mod-SDK-sdk-*.zip (public release sdk-2026.11.04.1 is about 600 MB). It contains the DLLs and local dependencies and opens without Git; GitHub's auto-generated Source code (zip) may only contain Git LFS pointers. Check the ZIP against the release’s SHA256SUMS.txt using the download verification steps. Then extract the whole archive into a new folder and keep the layout below. <your extract folder>/ ├─ Packages/ # SDK dependencies, sibling to UnityProject └─ UnityProject/ ├─ Assets/ ├─ Packages/ │ └─ manifest.json └─ ProjectSettings/ └─ ProjectVersion.txt The outer Packages folder supplies local dependencies the project references, while UnityProject/Packages/manifest.json declares the project's own dependencies. Keep both in place. For a Git checkout, follow the clone and LFS steps. 2. Check the project folder and version Open UnityProject and check that it contains Assets/, Packages/manifest.json, and ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt. Open ProjectVersion.txt and note m_EditorVersion. The verified public release sdk-2026.11.04.1 declares Unity 2022.3.62f1. For a later release, read m_EditorVersion from that download and follow the Unity version guide to install the same version. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Check the adjacent public SDK checkout for its declared editor version, sibling package dependency, and vehicle template. Set sdkCheckout to the outer directory if the SDK is elsewhere. [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.Directory/Exists", "args": [ "${sdkCheckout}/UnityProject/Assets" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/ReadAllText", "args": [ "${sdkCheckout}/UnityProject/ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "m_EditorVersion: 2022.3.62f1" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/ReadAllText", "args": [ "${sdkCheckout}/UnityProject/Packages/manifest.json" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "file:../../Packages/Sdk/com.shanghaiwindy.middlelayer" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/Exists", "args": [ "${sdkCheckout}/UnityProject/Assets/ModManager/BuildPipline-Template-Vehicle.asset" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/Exists", "args": [ "${sdkCheckout}/UnityProject/Assets/ModManager/Template-Blank-Vehicle.asset" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/Exists", "args": [ "${sdkCheckout}/Packages/Sdk/com.shanghaiwindy.middlelayer/package.json" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } } ] 3. Open the project in Unity Hub In Unity Hub, choose Projects → Add → Add project from disk and select UnityProject inside the extract folder, not the outer folder, Assets, or Packages. Check for the three paths listed in section 2 to identify the correct folder. Open the project from the list with the same editor version declared in ProjectVersion.txt. The first launch downloads packages, imports assets, and compiles scripts, so it takes much longer than later launches; wait for both Hub and Editor progress to finish. After compilation, check the Console for compile errors. With compilation complete, look for Framework - 框架 in the menu bar. If the menu is missing, check in order: that you opened the inner UnityProject, that the neighboring Packages folder is complete, that extraction finished, and that the editor version matches the declaration. If Hub reports a missing editor, install that version and open the project again. Common failures: opening the outer folder reports that it is not a Unity project; an incomplete extraction reports missing packages or DLLs; moving Packages away leaves local packages unresolved. 4. Verify your setup with a bundled template In File → Build Settings, choose the target platform. For Windows, choose PC, Mac & Linux Standalone → Windows → x86_64. For Android, choose Android. Click Switch Platform when needed. In Project, select Assets/ModManager/BuildPipline-Template-Vehicle.asset. Click Build Linked Objects to AssetBundle and wait for it to finish. Select Assets/ModManager/Template-Blank-Vehicle.asset and click Package Mod Now. The Windows example outputs to UnityProject/Build/Mod-Package/StandaloneWindows64/Template-Blank-Vehicle/. After changing assets or platform, build the linked objects again before packaging. Follow Install mods to add the .modpack for your game's platform. For a map template, use BuildPipline-Template-Blank.asset and Template-Blank-Scene.asset in the same Project folder. Packaging the template and loading it in the game confirms the project and editor setup. Next, set the Steam game folder if needed or build your first tank. If your GameHub build can create projects, you can use the GameHub workflow to open the result.

Generate external armor The second segment is the integer armor thickness. Use Inter for spaced armor and React for reactive armor.
