manual/en/mod/instalod-plugin.html.title: Generate vehicle LODs with InstaLOD | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/instalod-plugin.html.summary: Generate vehicle LODs with InstaLOD 中文 | English LOD generation ships with the mod SDK: its manifest already references the sibling package com.shanghaiwindy.simplygon, which embeds InstaLOD and InstaLodMeshProvider. You do not install anything by hand for the public SDK. The provider hosting LOD work is InstaLOD even though the package and field names say simplygon. Ordinary automatic LOD runs when VehicleData.isGenLOD is enabled. Advanced mode additionally requires both isPriorityAdvanceLOD and EditorStorage.useSimplygon to be true; useSimplygon defaults to false, so advanced mode is off until you turn it on. Enable isGenLOD on the vehicle data. For advanced reduction, authorize the plugin on this machine through Window → InstaLOD, then enable Priority Advance LOD for the vehicle and Use Insta Lod in the editor settings. If authorization fails, turn the editor setting off and repack with ordinary LOD generation. InstaLOD documentation Repack the vehicle so the pipeline runs. Inspect the generated prefab and read its LODGroup for the levels that were actually produced. Level count and naming depend on the asset; do not assume fixed node names. The screenshot sequence below is historical: package installation and configuration screens come from an older client. Do not treat their labels as current UI promises. Package Manager → Add package from disk, then pick the provider package.json; older SDKs also required provider authorization. Framework → Gm → Editor Config → Use Insta Lod, then Save. Repack, then Open Vehicle Data Tool → View Packed Asset. The default shared mesh output is Assets/Res/Cooked/SimplifiedMeshGroup. For a vehicle with a local cook directory, look for SimplifiedMeshGroup under that output directory. The older hull example used node suffixes 100, 75, 50, and 30. Check the generated LODGroup for its actual levels. For mesh editing outside the pipeline, see InstaLOD Studio.

manual/en/mod/instalod-studio.html.title: Reduce a mesh in InstaLOD Studio | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/instalod-studio.html.summary: Reduce a mesh in InstaLOD Studio 中文 | English InstaLOD Studio is an optional external tool for editing a mesh before it goes back into the project. Nothing in the build pipeline depends on it; you can use it on a copy of a vehicle or prop mesh when the geometry needs decimation or cleanup that is easier outside Unity. The vendor's Getting Started guide covers installation and the general workflow. The button and menu labels below are screenshot observations from an older session. Treat them as the sequence to expect, not as a promise about the names in the version you are running. 1. Set up a profile Start with a new profile: New Profile, choose the Optimize (AutoLow) template, then Create Profile. This gives you a decimation pipeline without assembling the operations by hand. Use File → Import Scene to load the mesh you want to work on. Work on a copy, so the original asset stays untouched. 2. Decide how far to reduce The historic session left the default quality settings alone for a first attempt. If you need more reduction than the template gives, it is optional to switch Automatic Quality off and enter a Percent Triangles value by hand, for example 20. The percentage is a target for the operation, not a guaranteed final ratio, so read the result rather than assuming it. 3. Run the operation and compare Press Start and let the pipeline finish, then compare the counts. In the observed example the scene went from 6,340 to 758 polygons and from 10,451 to 1,415 vertices. That is what that particular mesh produced with those settings; a different mesh or a different percentage will land elsewhere. Check the silhouette while the reduced mesh is still in the tool. A shape that looked acceptable at the original density can lose thin parts, flat panels or small details once the polygon count drops. 4. Export to a separate file Use File → Export Scene and write to a new file. Keeping the exported mesh separate from the source makes it easy to compare the two and to discard the result if something went wrong. 5. Reimport into Unity and inspect Import the exported file into a test folder in Unity and check it before replacing anything: Silhouette: the reduced shape still reads as the same object from the angles the player sees. Materials: the material assignments survived the export and still point at the intended surfaces. UVs: texture coordinates are intact, so textures do not stretch or slide on the reduced mesh. Pivots: the object's origin and orientation are where the project expects them, so turrets, guns, wheels and attachments still rotate and mount correctly. If any of these checks fails, adjust the settings and export again, or keep the original mesh and treat InstaLOD as a one-off experiment.

manual/en/mod/jenkins-setup.html.title: Build mods with a self-hosted Jenkins setup | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/jenkins-setup.html.summary: Build mods with a self-hosted Jenkins setup 中文 | English Use Jenkins to schedule a local build manifest on your own Windows build machine. The official mod repository uses GitHub Actions Build modpack. 1. Install the service and complete setup Install a Java version supported by your Jenkins LTS, then run its Windows MSI. Choose the installation directory. Use a local or domain account with Log on as a service permission, then select the Java home and port. Jenkins Windows installation Check that Jenkins is running in Windows Services. Use Restart there after changing the service configuration. Open the selected local port in a browser. The default is http://localhost:8080. On Unlock Jenkins, read the initialAdminPassword file from the shown location and enter it. Choose Install suggested plugins or Select plugins to install. Create the first administrator and open Jenkins. The Pipeline below calls Unity directly. Install other plugins as needed. 2. Prepare the build machine and manifest Install Git, Git LFS, the SDK's Unity version, and the target platform modules. Verify that the Jenkins service account can read the project and run Unity. Put the full path to the matching Unity.exe in the worker's UNITY_EXE environment variable. Commit the ModPackageBuildPiplineData asset and CI/ModBuild.json in the Unity project. Follow the manifest example and keep StandaloneWindows64 as its platform and Build/Ship/Windows as its destination. Begin with an empty output directory. Add Assets/Editor/CiModBuild.cs to the Unity project with this -executeMethod entry point. The caller passes the manifest path. using System; using System.IO; using ShanghaiWindy.Editor; public static class CiModBuild { public static void Run() { var args = Environment.GetCommandLineArgs(); var index = Array.IndexOf(args, "-modManifest"); if (index < 0 || index + 1 >= args.Length) { throw new ArgumentException("Supply -modManifest followed by the JSON path."); } Utility_BuildPipline.BuildPiplineManifest(Path.GetFullPath(args[index + 1])); } } 3. Create a Pipeline and check the build Save the script below as CI/Build-Mod.ps1 in the Unity project. Win64 is Unity 2022.3's command-line switch value. The manifest still uses StandaloneWindows64. Unity Editor command-line arguments $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop' $project = (Resolve-Path .).Path $manifest = Join-Path $project 'CI/ModBuild.json' $output = Join-Path $project 'Build/Ship/Windows' $log = Join-Path $project 'Build/UnityBuild.log' New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $output -Force | Out-Null if (Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $output -Filter '*.modpack' -File) { throw "Use a clean output directory before building: $output" } $arguments = @( '-batchmode', '-quit', '-projectPath', ('"' + $project + '"'), '-buildTarget', 'Win64', '-executeMethod', 'CiModBuild.Run', '-modManifest', ('"' + $manifest + '"'), '-logFile', ('"' + $log + '"') ) $build = Start-Process -FilePath $env:UNITY_EXE -ArgumentList $arguments -Wait -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden if ($build.ExitCode -ne 0) { throw "Unity exited with $($build.ExitCode). See $log" } if (-not (Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $output -Filter '*.modpack' -File)) { throw "No .modpack in $output. Check the manifest's target platform and directory." } Create a Jenkins Pipeline and select Pipeline script from SCM. Save the following Jenkinsfile at the repository root. Replace windows-unity with the label on your Windows agent. The Checkout stage resets this job's dedicated build workspace before cloning so each build has a fresh output directory. If the Unity project is in a subdirectory, wrap the PowerShell build step in dir('path/to/project') and prefix the archive patterns with that path. Jenkinsfile guide · PowerShell step pipeline { agent { label 'windows-unity' } options { skipDefaultCheckout() } stages { stage('Checkout') { steps { deleteDir() checkout scm bat 'git lfs pull' } } stage('Build mods') { steps { powershell '& ./CI/Build-Mod.ps1' archiveArtifacts artifacts: 'Build/Ship/Windows/*.modpack' } } } post { always { archiveArtifacts artifacts: 'Build/UnityBuild.log', allowEmptyArchive: true } } } Choose Build Now with a teaching mod. Open Build/UnityBuild.log from the artifacts and check the target, the names built, and the destination. Before distributing a successful build, create the matching .modpack.json using the manifest guide and keep it alongside the archive. Check each archive's GUID, version, and target.

manual/en/mod/lua-api2-air-warning.html.summary:
Warn when an enemy aircraft approaches 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run lua-api2-air-warning Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "script": "${fixture}/AirThreatWarning.lua", "prefab": "${fixture}/Tutorial_AirThreatWarning.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } This vehicle Lua behaviour logs a warning when an enemy aircraft comes within range of the local player. It can also play an FMOD warning. Start with Lua Hello World if you need help importing and attaching a script. 1. Import and configure the warning Create AirThreatWarning.lua under the Unity project's assets and copy the script below. In VehicleTextData → Misc → Vehicle Lua behavior, add a row, assign the script, and click Sync Properties. To bind through a prefab, add LuaBehaviorMono to an object in the owning vehicle hierarchy. Keep warnDistance at 3,000 m. Assign an FMOD event GUID to soundGuid, or leave it empty for the first log-only test. Save, repack, and test the vehicle. The script creates one query in OnVehicleReady and runs it every 0.5 seconds. Query field Value and use Kind VehicleKind.Flight matches aircraft. Other options include Any, Ground, and Army. Relation VehicleRelation.Enemy uses the team of the vehicle passed to Run(vehicle). Other values include Any and Friendly. MaxDistance warnDistance, measured in metres. A value of 0 removes that distance limit. MaxCount 1, so the sorted result contains only the nearest aircraft. The default capacity is 32. SortByDistance true, so the nearest result comes first. Behavior() Property = { warnDistance = { type = "number", value = 3000 }, soundGuid = { type = "string", value = "" }, } local AirThreatWarning = class("AirThreatWarning") function AirThreatWarning:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) self.vehicle = vehicle self.query = VehicleAPI.CreateQuery() self.query.Kind = VehicleKind.Flight self.query.Relation = VehicleRelation.Enemy self.query.MaxDistance = self.warnDistance self.query.MaxCount = 1 self.query.SortByDistance = true self.warned = false self.script:SetUpdateInterval(0.5) end function AirThreatWarning:OnUpdated() if self.query == nil or not VehicleAPI.IsLocalPlayer(self.vehicle) then return end local count = self.query:Run(self.vehicle) if count == 0 then self.warned = false return end if self.warned then return end local nearest = self.query:Get(0) if nearest == nil then return end self.warned = true print(string.format("[AirWarning] %s at %.0f m", VehicleAPI.GetDisplayName(nearest), self.query:GetDistance(0))) if self.soundGuid ~= "" then SoundAPI.PlayOneShot(self.soundGuid, self.transform.position) end end return AirThreatWarning Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/ImportAsset", "args": [ "${script}", "ForceSynchronousImport" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": Check when the warning repeats Drive the vehicle as the local player in the playground. Bring a visible enemy aircraft into range. Look for [AirWarning] followed by the nearest aircraft's name and distance. The script reads the first result with Get(0) and GetDistance(0). The warning should run once while detections remain in range. When the query becomes empty, the next detection can trigger it again. If you added a sound GUID, check that it plays at the vehicle's position. Check the local player, teams, and visibility. Online results follow team visibility. For scripts on maps or game modes, use RunAt(position, team) to query around a point for a chosen team. Older scripts polled scene rigidbodies and filtered aircraft in Lua. This example keeps one query and performs the filtering and sorting in the game. The MCP replay simulates a target appearing, remaining in range, and leaving. Check the actual sound and online visibility in game. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Core.AssetBundleManager/LuaEnv/DoString", "args": [ "local E = setmetatable({ Behavior = function() end, class = function() return {} end, print = function() end }, { __index = _G })
local count, played, checks, localPlayer = 0, 0, 0, true
local aircraft = {}
local query = {
 Run = function() checks = checks + 1; return count end,
 Get = function(_, i) assert(i == 0); return aircraft end,
 GetDistance = function(_, i) assert(i == 0); return 500 end,
}
E.VehicleKind = { Flight = 2 }
E.VehicleRelation = { Enemy = 1 }
E.VehicleAPI = {
 CreateQuery = function() return query end,
 IsLocalPlayer = function() return localPlayer end,
 GetDisplayName = function(v) assert(v == aircraft); return "Sample" end,

Add a charge bonus to the primary weapon 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run lua-api2-charged-shot Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "script": "${fixture}/ChargedShot.lua", "prefab": "${fixture}/Tutorial_ChargedShot.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } 1. Import the script and attach it to a vehicle Create ChargedShot.lua in your Lua source folder and copy in the script below. Follow Lua Hello World to import it into Unity, then add the asset to the vehicle-level Lua behaviours in VehicleTextData. For a test prefab, you can also attach it with LuaBehaviorMono on an object in the vehicle hierarchy. Keep chargeTime = 4 seconds and maxBonus = 0.5 for the first test. The example uses weapon index 0. To pick another weapon, check the available count with WeaponAPI.GetWeaponCount and change the index. The script disables periodic updates if the weapon is missing or charge time is zero or negative. Use BuffAPI.CreateValueBuff to attach one mutable buff to the weapon's DamageBuffedCoff. Passing false for the second argument makes it additive. A value of 0.5 adds 50%. Passing true gives a multiplier that stacks multiplicatively. Keep one object and use SetValue to update it. An unchanged value leaves it as-is. On destruction, remove it with RemoveBuff. Behavior() Property = { maxBonus = { type = "number", value = 0.5 }, chargeTime = { type = "number", value = 4 }, } local ChargedShot = class("ChargedShot") function ChargedShot:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) local weapon = WeaponAPI.GetWeapon(vehicle, 0) if weapon == nil or self.chargeTime <= 0 then self.script:SetUpdateEnabled(false) return end self.weapon = weapon self.damage = weapon.DamageBuffedCoff self.charge = 0 self.buff = BuffAPI.CreateValueBuff("Charged Shot", false, 0) self.damage:AddBuff(self.buff) WeaponAPI.OnFired(self.script, weapon, function() self.charge = 0 self.buff:SetValue(0) end) self.script:SetUpdateInterval(0.1) end function ChargedShot:OnUpdated(dt) if self.buff == nil or not WeaponAPI.IsReloaded(self.weapon) then return end self.charge = math.min(self.charge + dt / self.chargeTime, 1) self.buff:SetValue(self.charge * self.maxBonus) end function ChargedShot:OnDestroyed() if self.buff ~= nil then self.damage:RemoveBuff(self.buff) self.buff = nil end end return ChargedShot Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": Engine RPM and landing gear 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run lua-api2-engine-gear Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "script": "${fixture}/EngineAndGear.lua", "prefab": "${fixture}/Tutorial_EngineAndGear.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } Attach the script to a vehicle. Assign fan, smoke or gearLights as needed. On aircraft, read the initial gear state and update the lights with FlightAPI.OnGearChanged. Pass self.script as the subscription owner and turn off per-frame updates for this branch. The ground branch uses TankAPI.GetEngineState, which returns success, RPM, RPM percentage, gear, speed and reverse status. The RPM percentage runs from 0 to 100; multiply RPM by 6 to get degrees per second. Speed is in km/h and is negative in reverse for tracked and wheeled vehicles. Tracked vehicles report first gear as 1 and reverse as 0. A wheeled vehicle without a gearbox reports RPM 0 and gear 1. Ships report RPM and speed, always gear 1 and reversing false. Fixed vehicles report RPM and speed 0, gear 1. The example scales the fan speed by 0.1 and shows smoke above 80 percent RPM. FlightAPI.IsOnGround checks ground contact. With the gear down, it can also run one physics overlap per wheel and return true for nearby ground or buildings. Limit the frequency of this physics query if the visual update runs often. Behavior() Property = { fan = { type = "object", value = nil }, smoke = { type = "object", value = nil }, gearLights = { type = "object", value = nil }, } local EngineAndGear = class("EngineAndGear") function EngineAndGear:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) self.vehicle = vehicle if VehicleAPI.IsFlightVehicle(vehicle) then if self.gearLights ~= nil then self.gearLights:SetActive(FlightAPI.IsGearDown(vehicle)) FlightAPI.OnGearChanged(self.script, vehicle, function(isDown) self.gearLights:SetActive(isDown) end) end self.vehicle = nil self.script:SetUpdateEnabled(false) return end self.script:SetUpdateEnabled(self.fan ~= nil or self.smoke ~= nil) end function EngineAndGear:OnUpdated(dt) if self.vehicle == nil then return end local ok, rpm, rpmPercent = TankAPI.GetEngineState(self.vehicle) if not ok then return end if self.fan ~= nil then self.fan.transform:Rotate(0, 0, rpm * 6 * dt * 0.1) end if self.smoke ~= nil then self.smoke:SetActive(rpmPercent > 80) end end return EngineAndGear Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/Copy", Match the missile rack models to the ammo count 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run lua-api2-missile-rack Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "script": "${fixture}/MissileRack.lua", "prefab": "${fixture}/Tutorial_MissileRack.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } Attach the script to the vehicle model and add children such as Missile_1 and Missile_2 in hierarchy order. Set weaponIndex and the text to match in object names, modelPrefix. The default index 1 selects the second weapon. Use 0 for the first. modelPrefix matches a case-sensitive substring anywhere in the name, so choose text unique to this group of models. The script calls TransformAPI.FindAllDeep once in OnVehicleReady to cache matched descendants in hierarchy order, including inactive objects. It then shows the first models in the list according to the weapon's current ammo count. WeaponAPI.OnAmmoChanged refreshes the display when ammo is spent or replenished. Subscribing with self.script ties the callback to the script's lifetime, so the subscription is removed automatically on destruction; there is no OnUpdated polling. When ammo decreases, the models at the end disappear first. Behavior() Property = { weaponIndex = { type = "number", value = 1 }, modelPrefix = { type = "string", value = "Missile_" }, } local MissileRack = class("MissileRack") function MissileRack:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) self.weapon = WeaponAPI.GetWeapon(vehicle, self.weaponIndex) if self.weapon == nil then return end self.models = TransformAPI.FindAllDeep(self.transform, self.modelPrefix) self:Refresh() WeaponAPI.OnAmmoChanged(self.script, self.weapon, function() self:Refresh() end) end function MissileRack:Refresh() local left = WeaponAPI.GetTotalAmmo(self.weapon) for index = 0, self.models.Length - 1 do self.models[index].gameObject:SetActive(index < left) end end return MissileRack Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/Copy", "args": [ "../../Docs/Manual/tutorials/lua-api2-missile-rack/example.lua", "${script}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/ImportAsset", "args": [ "${script}", "ForceSynchronousImport" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${prefab}", "mode": "create", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.Lua.LuaBehaviorMono", "children": [ "Missile_1", "Missile_2" ], "references": [ { "property": "luaBehavior", "asset": "${script}", "type": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.Lua.LuaBehaviorScript" } ], "values": { "instanceLuaProperty": { "numberProperties": [ { "variableName": "weaponIndex", "value": 1 } ], "stringProperties": [ { "variableName": "modelPrefix", "value": "Missile_" } ] } } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${prefab}/LuaBehaviorMono/luaBehavior/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "(String) MissileRack" } } ] The replay checks the initial count, consumption and resupply logic. Trigger an animation when a module is destroyed 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run lua-api2-module-trigger Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "script": "${fixture}/ModuleDestroyedTrigger.lua", "prefab": "${fixture}/Tutorial_ModuleDestroyedTrigger.prefab", "controller": "${fixture}/ModuleAnimator.controller" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } Use this example to play an animation when an internal module such as the ammo rack or engine is destroyed. You could open a hatch or play an engine fire effect. The script responds to module events and avoids reading hit points every frame. 1. Configure the Animator and attach the script Open the damage model in Prefab Mode. Put the object to animate inside that prefab, such as a child of the module. Add an Animator and assign an Animator Controller. In Animator → Parameters, choose + → Trigger and add Destroyed. Create the target animation state and set Destroyed as its transition condition. Import the Lua script below. Add LuaBehaviorMono to the object containing the internal module and assign the script. Drag the object with the Animator into animator. Set triggerName to the exact spelling and case used in the controller. Save the prefab. The script resolves the module in OnVehicleReady. In OnStarted, the damage model might still be assembling. If your test does not trigger the animation, check that the script and module share the same object and that animator is assigned. Behavior() Property = { animator = { type = "object", value = nil }, triggerName = { type = "string", value = "Destroyed" }, } local ModuleDestroyedTrigger = class("ModuleDestroyedTrigger") function ModuleDestroyedTrigger:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) local module = InternalModuleAPI.GetInternalModule(self.gameObject) if module == nil or self.animator == nil then return end local animator = ComponentAPI.GetNativeComponent(self.animator, "Animator") if animator == nil then return end local wasDestroyed = InternalModuleAPI.IsDestroyed(module) InternalModuleAPI.OnStateChanged(self.script, module, function() local destroyed = InternalModuleAPI.IsDestroyed(module) if destroyed and not wasDestroyed then animator:SetTrigger(self.triggerName) end wasDestroyed = destroyed end) end return ModuleDestroyedTrigger Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/Copy", "args": [ "../../Docs/Manual/tutorials/lua-api2-module-trigger/example.lua", "${script}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/ImportAsset", "args": [ "${script}", "ForceSynchronousImport" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Core.AssetBundleManager/LuaEnv/DoString", "args": [ "local e, u = CS.UnityEditor, CS.UnityEngine

controller:AddParameter("Destroyed", u.AnimatorControllerParameterType.Trigger)

return "Destroyed Animator trigger and transition configured"

Choose lifecycle callbacks and an update interval Callback When it runs OnStarted() The script instance starts. Its vehicle may still be assembling. OnVehicleReady(vehicle) Once after the owning vehicle is assembled, including in the garage. If the vehicle is already assembled when the script starts, this follows the startup routine. Standalone map and effect behaviours have no owning vehicle. OnUpdated(dt) Once per frame by default, or at the configured interval. dt is the accumulated time in seconds since the previous call. OnVehicleDestroyed(vehicle) The owning vehicle is killed. Use it for a destruction animation or cleanup. OnDestroyed() The behaviour instance is destroyed. Release resources managed by the script here. The game disposes of subscriptions owned by this behaviour afterward. Tank, turret, and tank weapon behaviours configured in vehicle data receive self.vehicle before OnStarted. Turret behaviours also receive self.turretController, tank weapon behaviours receive self.tankFire, and aircraft weapon behaviours receive self.flightFire. See vehicle initialization timing. Method Use self.script:GetVehicle() Gets and caches the owning tank, aircraft, or infantry unit. Returns nil for behaviours with no owning vehicle. self.script:SetUpdateInterval(seconds) Spreads out calls to OnUpdated. Pass 0 to run on every frame again. self.script:SetUpdateEnabled(false) Stops OnUpdated while keeping event callbacks and OnGUI available. Pass true to resume. 3. Subscribe to state changes Get a weapon in OnVehicleReady and subscribe to its ammo updates. Read ammo once for the initial display, then refresh it on OnAmmoChanged. Add the code below to the battle branch in the first example and draw self.ammo in OnGUI. local weapon = WeaponAPI.GetWeapon(vehicle, 0) if weapon then self.ammo = WeaponAPI.GetTotalAmmo(weapon) self.ammoSubscription = WeaponAPI.OnAmmoChanged(self.script, weapon, function() self.ammo = WeaponAPI.GetTotalAmmo(weapon) end) end self.script owns the subscription. Destroying the behaviour or removing an associated target vehicle ends it. To stop early, check that the subscription object exists and call sub:Dispose(). Repeat calls are safe. sub.IsActive tells you whether the subscription is still registered. A game mode or library script can pass nil as the owner. Subscriptions with a target follow the target's lifetime. Subscriptions with neither an owner nor a target end when the game mode exits. The game stops invoking a subscription callback after 10 consecutive errors. Check the event name and script context in the game log to locate the error. 4. Find the API and handle return values Class Purpose and common methods VehicleAPI Vehicle identity, state, queries, and events. GetContext, IsGarage, IsLocalPlayer, IsBot, IsRemote, IsAlive, GetTeam, IsEnemy, GetDisplayName, GetGuid, GetVelocity, GetSpeedKmh, GetAimPoint, CreateQuery, OnVehicleSpawned, OnVehicleKilled. RadarAPI Ground and airborne radars. TryGetRadar, IsActive, GetWorkMode, GetScanAzimuth, GetContactCount, GetContact, GetContactWorldAzimuth, GetLockedTarget, TryLock, Unlock, OnLockChanged, OnThreat. WeaponAPI Weapons, ammo, reloads, lead, and events. GetWeaponCount, GetWeapon, GetAmmo, GetTotalAmmo, IsReloaded, GetReloadProgress, GetReloadTime, GetMuzzle, GetShellSpeed, PredictLead, OnFired, OnAmmoChanged, OnReloaded, OnHit, OnKill. TankAPI Turret and engine. GetTurretCount, GetTurretTransform, GetGunTransform, GetEngineState. FlightAPI Flight state and landing gear. IsOnGround, IsGearDown, GetAirspeedKmh, GetAltitude, GetThrottle, IsEngineRunning, OnGearChanged. InternalModuleAPI Internal modules. GetInternalModule, IsDestroyed, GetHitPointRatio, OnStateChanged, OnDamaged, OnRepaired. CameraAPI Player camera. GetCameraMode, IsZoomed, GetLockTarget. TransformAPI Model nodes. FindDeep, FindAllDeep. BuffAPI Create a buff with an editable value using CreateValueBuff. TimeAPI Check the pause state with IsPaused. Find the signatures in ShanghaiWindy.Core.API or use the SDK hints in VS Code after setting up EmmyLua. C# arrays and contact indices start at zero. For methods with out values such as TryGetRadar or GetContact, first check the boolean result in Lua. Handle missing results according to each signature, such as nil, false, or 0. Distances are generally in metres and angles in degrees. Check the method's speed units. For example, GetSpeedKmh returns kilometres per hour. Online battle queries filter enemy vehicles by team visibility. Radar contacts are subject to detection. To control a radar, use the vehicle currently controlled by the player and check the result of methods such as TryLock. Display radar contacts in a mod 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run lua-api2-radar-screen Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. Configure the ground radar Select the vehicle's VehicleTextData. Under Misc → AA Radar, expand groundAARadarData and enable hasRadar. The replay uses a 12,000 m detection range, 360° rotating search, and a rotation rate of 60°/s. For a directional radar, turn full rotation off and adjust the azimuth and elevation half angles. Field Meaning maxDetectionRange Maximum detection range in metres isFullRotation, fullRotationRate Full-rotation search and its rate in degrees per second searchAzimuthHalfAngle, searchElevationHalfAngle Half angles of the search region. The defaults are 45° / 30°. minElevationAngle, detectGroundTargets The ground-clutter filter defaults to 2° minimum elevation. Allowing ground contacts skips this filter. Range and scan coverage still apply. displayRanges The default display scales are 2,500 / 5,000 / 10,000 / 20,000 m. canUsePD, pdMinDetectableSpeed Pulse-Doppler mode and its speed threshold. The default threshold is 30 m/s. hasIFF Show friendly returns and mark them as friendly. Bind the script and update the list Save the script below as RadarScreen.lua and import it. On a child object of the vehicle prefab, add LuaBehaviorMono, assign the script to Behavior, save, and repack. LuaBehaviorMono walkthrough OnVehicleReady obtains the radar and subscribes to lock changes. The example refreshes contact text every 0.2 seconds. Unity can call OnGUI several times per frame, so it draws the cached text. Read the latest scan's contacts from index 0 to GetContactCount(radar) - 1. GetContact returns success, target, distance, azimuth, elevation, altitude, radial speed, and friendly status in that order. A chaff return has a nil target. Distance and altitude use metres, and radial speed uses m/s. Azimuth and elevation use the radar's frame of reference. Use GetContactWorldAzimuth for a north-up display. Use GetScanAzimuth for antenna yaw relative to its mount, from −180° to 180°. Behavior() Property = {} local RadarScreen = class("RadarScreen") local GUI = CS.UnityEngine.GUI local Rect = CS.UnityEngine.Rect function RadarScreen:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) local ok, radar = RadarAPI.TryGetRadar(vehicle) if not ok then self.script:SetUpdateEnabled(false) return end self.vehicle = vehicle self.radar = radar self.lines = {} self.text = "" RadarAPI.OnLockChanged(self.script, radar, function(locked, target) if locked and target ~= nil then print("[Radar] locked " .. VehicleAPI.GetDisplayName(target)) elseif not locked then print("[Radar] lock lost") end end) self.script:SetUpdateInterval(0.2) end function RadarScreen:OnUpdated() self.visible = self.radar ~= nil and VehicleAPI.IsLocalPlayer(self.vehicle) and RadarAPI.IsActive(self.radar) if not self.visible then return end local written = 0 for index = 0, RadarAPI.GetContactCount(self.radar) - 1 do local ok, target, distance, azimuth, elevation, altitude, radialSpeed, isFriendly = RadarAPI.GetContact(self.radar, index) if ok then local name = target ~= nil and VehicleAPI.GetDisplayName(target) or "?" local bearing = RadarAPI.GetContactWorldAzimuth(self.radar, index) written = written + 1 self.lines[written] = string.format("%s %s %.1f km %03.0f° %.0f m", isFriendly and "+" or "!", name, distance / 1000, bearing, altitude) end end for index = written + 1, #self.lines do self.lines[index] = nil end self.text = table.concat(self.lines, "
") end function RadarScreen:OnGUI() if self.visible then GUI.Label(Rect(20, 120, 360, 300), self.text) end end return RadarScreen Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/Copy", "args": [ "../../Docs/Manual/tutorials/lua-api2-radar-screen/example.lua", "${script}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/ImportAsset", "args": [ "${script}", "ForceSynchronousImport" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${prefab}", "mode": "create", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.Lua.LuaBehaviorMono", "children": [], "references": [ { "property": "luaBehavior", "asset": "${script}", "type": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.Lua.LuaBehaviorScript" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${prefab}/LuaBehaviorMono/luaBehavior/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "(String) RadarScreen" } } ] 3. Turn radar off and check that the list disappears. Remote-player replicas do not scan on the local client. TryLock, Unlock, CycleTarget, and SwitchMode operate on the locally controlled vehicle. TryLock needs a contact on the radar scope and still takes the normal acquisition time. The script prints a [Radar] entry when the lock is acquired or lost. The MCP replay checks configuration, script binding, the missing-radar case, chaff display, expired rows, and list hiding when the radar is inactive. Detection and locking need an in-game scene. This example checks the import and binding of a minimal behavior asset. 1. Create the behavior script Save ExampleBehavior.lua under an asset folder in the Unity project. The project importer recognizes Behavior() as the behavior marker. Files under a LuaProject path are imported as plain text. Drag the imported ExampleBehavior asset from the Project window into the Behavior field. That field takes the imported behavior asset, not the raw .lua text file. If the script declares a Property table, use Sync Variable Property Definition to add missing instance fields, then set the value of each field on this instance. API 2 creates a mutable coefficient with BuffAPI.CreateValueBuff and adds it to the main weapon's ReloadTimeBuffedCoff. The example adds it with F1 and removes it with F2. With no other reload modifiers, -0.5 changes an eight-second reload to four seconds. Destroying the behaviour unregisters the keys and removes the attached buff. Behavior() Property = { reloadCoefficient = { type = "number", value = -0.5 }, } local ReloadBuffExample = class("ReloadBuffExample") function ReloadBuffExample:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) if not VehicleAPI.IsLocalPlayer(vehicle) then return end local weapon = WeaponAPI.GetWeapon(vehicle, 0) if weapon == nil then return end self.stat = weapon.ReloadTimeBuffedCoff self.buff = BuffAPI.CreateValueBuff("Example reload time", false, self.reloadCoefficient) local id = tostring(self.gameObject:GetInstanceID()) self.addAction = "ExampleReloadAdd_" .. id self.removeAction = "ExampleReloadRemove_" .. id InputAPI.RegisterKeyInput(self.addAction, "F1", function() self:Add() end, function() end) InputAPI.RegisterKeyInput(self.removeAction, "F2", function() self:Remove() end, function() end) end function ReloadBuffExample:Add() if self.buff ~= nil and not self.added then self.stat:AddBuff(self.buff) self.added = true end end function ReloadBuffExample:Remove() if self.added then self.stat:RemoveBuff(self.buff) self.added = false end end function ReloadBuffExample:OnDestroyed() if self.addAction ~= nil then InputAPI.UnregisterKeyInput(self.addAction) InputAPI.UnregisterKeyInput(self.removeAction) end self:Remove() end return ReloadBuffExample Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": Save the code below as RandomSpawn.lua, import it into Unity, and assign it to the component. Assign a meteor prefab to prefab in the Lua object properties. The example uses count, fieldSize, and noiseScale to control the object count, XZ range, and height variation. Start with a small number of objects. Behavior() Property = { prefab = { type = "object", value = nil }, count = { type = "number", value = 100 }, fieldSize = { type = "number", value = 100 }, noiseScale = { type = "number", value = 10 } } local RandomSpawn = class("RandomSpawn") local Mathf = CS.UnityEngine.Mathf local Vector3 = CS.UnityEngine.Vector3 local Quaternion = CS.UnityEngine.Quaternion function RandomSpawn:OnStarted() if self.prefab == nil then return end local count = math.max(0, math.floor(self.count or 100)) local fieldSize = math.max(0, self.fieldSize or 100) local noiseScale = math.max(0.01, self.noiseScale or 10) for i = 1, count do local x = math.random() * fieldSize local z = math.random() * fieldSize local y = Mathf.PerlinNoise(x / noiseScale, z / noiseScale) * fieldSize local meteor = CS.UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate(self.prefab, Vector3(x, y, z), Quaternion.identity) meteor.name = "Meteor_" .. i end end return RandomSpawn Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ manual/en/mod/lua-self-dot-vs-colon.html.title: Dot and colon in Lua method calls | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/lua-self-dot-vs-colon.html.summary:
Dot and colon in Lua method calls 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run lua-self-dot-vs-colon item:add(3) passes item as the first argument. It is equivalent to item.add(item, 3). In function item:add(n), the first parameter is implicitly named self. Use a dot for ordinary functions that receive no instance. Compare the calls in Lua local item = { total = 2 } function item:add(n) return self.total + n end assert(item:add(3) == 5) assert(item.add(item, 3) == 5) assert(math.abs(-3) == 3) With item.add(3), Lua assigns 3 to self and leaves n without an argument. To pass a method to an event, see Keep self in a Lua callback. Vehicle initialization timing 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run lua-vehicle-init-timing Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "script": "${fixture}/VehicleTiming.lua", "prefab": "${fixture}/Tutorial_VehicleTiming.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } On Lua API 2 or later, put code that needs assembled vehicle components in OnVehicleReady. The script runs OnStarted first. If the vehicle is already assembled, OnVehicleReady follows immediately. Otherwise it runs once after assembly. Bind the script to a LuaBehaviorMono on the vehicle. Put your component setup in InitVehicleDependencies. On older clients, resolve the vehicle with TryGetTankInitSystem, then check IsLoaded or subscribe to the loaded event. The example removes its legacy subscription when the behaviour is destroyed. Behavior() Property = {} local VehicleTiming = class("VehicleTiming") function VehicleTiming:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) if vehicle == nil or self.vehicle ~= nil then return end self.vehicle = vehicle self:InitVehicleDependencies() end function VehicleTiming:InitVehicleDependencies() print("[VehicleTiming] vehicle is ready") end function VehicleTiming:OnStarted() if (GAME_API_VERSION or 1) >= 2 then return end local found, vehicle = self.script:TryGetTankInitSystem() if not found or vehicle == nil then return end if vehicle.IsLoaded then self:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) return end self.legacyVehicle = vehicle self.legacyLoaded = function() self:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) end VehicleAPI.RegisterVehicleLoadedEvent(vehicle, self.legacyLoaded) end function VehicleTiming:OnDestroyed() if self.legacyLoaded ~= nil then VehicleAPI.UnRegisterVehicleLoaedEvent(self.legacyVehicle, self.legacyLoaded) self.legacyVehicle = nil self.legacyLoaded = nil end end return VehicleTiming Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/Copy", "args": [ "../../Docs/Manual/tutorials/lua-vehicle-init-timing/example.lua", "${script}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/ImportAsset", "args": [ "${script}", "ForceSynchronousImport" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${prefab}", "mode": "create", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.Lua.LuaBehaviorMono", "children": [], "references": [ { "property": "luaBehavior", "asset": "${script}", "type": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.Lua.LuaBehaviorScript" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${prefab}/LuaBehaviorMono/luaBehavior/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "(String) VehicleTiming" } } ] The replay checks that API 2 skips the legacy subscription, and that the legacy path waits and unregisters. Check actual assembly timing in game. local subscriptions, removals, inits = 0, 0, 0
local callback
E.VehicleAPI = {
 RegisterVehicleLoadedEvent = function(v, cb) subscriptions = subscriptions + 1; callback = cb end,
 UnRegisterVehicleLoaedEvent = function(v, cb) assert(cb == callback); removals = removals + 1 end
}

local B = assert(loadfile('../../Docs/Manual/tutorials/lua-vehicle-init-timing/example.lua', 't', E))()
local function instance(t) return setmetatable(t, { __index = B }) end
local vehicle = { IsLoaded = false }
local script = { TryGetTankInitSystem = function() return true, vehicle end }
local init = function() inits = inits + 1 end
E.GAME_API_VERSION = 2
local current = instance({ script = script, InitVehicleDependencies = init })
current:OnStarted()
assert(subscriptions == 0 and current.vehicle == nil)
current:OnVehicleReady(vehicle)
current:OnVehicleReady(vehicle)
assert(inits == 1 and current.vehicle == vehicle)
E.GAME_API_VERSION = nil

legacy:OnStarted()
assert(subscriptions == 1 and legacy.vehicle == nil)
callback()
callback()
assert(inits == 2 and legacy.vehicle == vehicle)
legacy:OnDestroyed()
assert(removals == 1)

manual/en/mod/map-asset-download.html.title: Map projects and asset sources | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/map-asset-download.html.summary: Map projects and asset sources 中文 | English Create a map with the public SDK Follow project setup to download the release ZIP and open UnityProject in Unity Hub. Locate Assets/Template-Scene in Project. Follow the map wizard to create your own scene. To verify your setup first, select BuildPipline-Template-Blank.asset in Assets/ModManager and build its linked objects. Then select Template-Blank-Scene.asset and package it. Build Windows and Android separately and install the .modpack for your game's platform. Multi-platform builds Maintain official maps and DIY parts Maintainers with access can clone the official mods repository and keep Projects and Packages in their original layout. Follow the official asset workflow to fetch the required Git LFS files, then open Projects/Maps. Its Packages/manifest.json resolves local UPM dependencies from the same repository. Official mods repository Content Repository path Official maps Packages/Maps/<pack>, for example Packages/Maps/Provisional DIY map parts Packages/Maps/DIYBuildings, Packages/Maps/DIYJapaneseBuildings, and Packages/Maps/DIYOfficial Shared dependencies Packages/Maps/Shared and the dependencies listed in each map pack's package.json In Unity's Project window, expand Packages to find the assets. Keep .meta files alongside the scenes and assets you edit. Create a work branch and use git status to check which packages, dependencies, and .meta files changed. For shared assets, check the upstream source before committing and requesting review. Official asset workflow Identify paths from the earlier project layout OfficialURPMaps, com.shanghaiwindy.urpmaps/Scenes, and com.shanghaiwindy.diymapconfigs refer to the earlier layout. The old instructions placed three GitLab checkouts for the vehicle project, maps, and shared resources under one parent folder. Use those names when tracking down historic assets. For current maps and DIY parts, use the unified repository paths above.

manual/en/mod/material-component.html.title: Configure Vehicle Material Overrides | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/material-component.html.summary: Configure Vehicle Material Overrides 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run material-component --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "material": "${fixture}/Tutorial_Prop.mat", "settings": "${fixture}/Tutorial_MaterialSettings.asset", "model": "${fixture}/Tutorial_Material.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } This example configures transparency in the DE client project. In the public SDK, follow project setup to select the Unity version declared by the SDK. CoreRPMatData stores material parameters. CoreRPMatComponent supplies those parameters when the vehicle's resources load. 1. Prepare the source material Find the target Mesh Renderer in the model prefab and identify its material slot. The recipe copies an existing propeller material to Tutorial_Prop.mat and assigns it to the first slot of Tutorial_Material.prefab. For your own model, use its mesh and textures. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/Altius-U/Art/Default-FastProp.mat", "${material}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${model}", "mode": "create", "component": "UnityEngine.MeshRenderer", "values": { "m_Materials": [ {} ] }, "references": [ { "property": "m_Materials.Array.data[0]", "asset": "${material}", "type": "UnityEngine.Material" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 2. Create the material configuration In the Project window, choose Create > A Panzer War - 装甲纷争 > C Config - 配置 > SRP Material Config - SRP 材质配置 to create CoreRPMatData. Expand coreRPMatParams and add an entry. Set coreRPShaderType to Transparency. Expand transparencyMatParam. Set the color's alpha to 0.35 and smoothness to 0.4. Assign the same Material asset used by the Mesh Renderer slot to linkedMaterial. For a camouflage setup, select VehicleCamouflage. The hasMask and maskTex fields in vehicleCamoflageMatParam supply the mask to the selected shader. Consult that shader for its channel meanings. On the source material, check the base texture _BaseMap, normal texture _BumpMap, and mask _MaskMap. Vehicle camouflage can inherit the source material's _MaskMap. To override that texture for this configuration, enable hasMask and assign maskTex. Use the mask preview to inspect channels individually. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateAsset", "args": [ "@static:UnityEngine.ScriptableObject/CreateInstance(ShanghaiWindy.Core.Data.CoreRPMatData)", "${settings}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${settings}/coreRPMatParams", "value": "[{\"coreRPShaderType\": 1, \"transparencyMatParam\": {\"color\": {\"r\": 1, \"g\": 1, \"b\": 1, \"a\": 0.35}, \"smoothness\": 0.4}}]" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${settings}/coreRPMatParams/0/linkedMaterial", "value": "@asset:${material}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 3. Attach the component Add CoreRPMatComponent to the target object. Leave isComponentBased off and assign Tutorial_MaterialSettings to matData. Multiple renderers can reuse this configuration. The component mode instead uses each indexCoreRPMatParams entry's index to select a slot on the same object's Mesh Renderer. Counting starts at zero. Check those indices when reordering material slots. The index resolves to the Material asset assigned to the slot. Other renderers that share the same material in the same conversion can inherit the override. To change a single slot, duplicate the material and assign the copy to that slot before setting its index. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${model}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.CoreRPMatComponent", "values": { "isComponentBased": false }, "references": [ { "property": "matData", "asset": "${settings}", "type": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.Data.CoreRPMatData" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 4. Save and check the references Save the prefab and read back the Mesh Renderer material, linkedMaterial and component matData references. During resource loading, the code matches the source Material object and applies the parameters to an instance. Check the visual result after loading the vehicle. This example verifies the editor assets and their parameters. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/MeshRenderer/sharedMaterials/0/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "Tutorial_Prop" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${settings}/coreRPMatParams/0/linkedMaterial/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "Tutorial_Prop" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/CoreRPMatComponent/matData/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "Tutorial_MaterialSettings" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${settings}/coreRPMatParams/0/transparencyMatParam/color/a" }, "expect": { "contains": "0.35" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${settings}/coreRPMatParams/0/transparencyMatParam/smoothness" }, "expect": { "contains": "0.4" } } ]

manual/en/mod/merge-texture-channels.htm.summary:
Merge PBR mask channels 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run merge-texture-channels In the mod SDK's GM Editor, open Remap PBR Masks. Assign metallic, occlusion, and smoothness. If you have a roughness map, put it in the smoothness slot and enable Is Roughness. Select Create Mask Map and save a PNG. The output uses the metallic texture's dimensions, or 512 × 512 if you omit metallic. Output channel Source R Red channel of metallic G Green channel of occlusion B 0 A Red channel of smoothness, transformed by the tool. For roughness, the tool inverts the transformed value Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEngine.SystemInfo/graphicsDeviceName" }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Standalone shader check in DE. It needs an adjacent Panzer-War-Mod-SDK checkout and an unused TutorialMaskTest folder. [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "Assets", "TutorialMaskTest" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/Copy", "args": [ "../../../Panzer-War-Mod-SDK/Packages/Sdk/com.shanghaiwindy.middlelayer/Tools/TextureMergeTool/Editor/MaskMap.shader", "Assets/TutorialMaskTest/SDKMask.shader" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/ImportAsset", "args": [ "Assets/TutorialMaskTest/SDKMask.shader", "ForceSynchronousImport" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Core.AssetBundleManager/LuaEnv/DoString", "args": [ "local U = CS.UnityEngine
local function texture(r, g)
 local image = U.Texture2D(2, 2, U.TextureFormat.RGBA32, false, true)
 for x = 0, 1 do
 for y = 0, 1 do
 image:SetPixel(x, y, U.Color(r, g, 0, 1))
 end
 end
 image:Apply()
 return image
end
local shader = U.Shader.Find("Hidden/MaskMap")
assert(shader and shader.isSupported, 'SDK MaskMap shader did not import')
local material = U.Material(shader)
local metal, ao, smooth = texture(0.25, 0.4), texture(0.1, 0.75), texture(0.48, 0.8)
local readout = texture(0, 0)
local target = U.RenderTexture(2, 2, 0, U.RenderTextureFormat.ARGB32, U.RenderTextureReadWrite.Linear)
local active = U.RenderTexture.active
local ok, failure = pcall(function()
 material:SetTexture("_Metallic", metal)
 material:SetTexture("_Occlusion", ao)
 material:SetTexture("_Smoothness", smooth)
 for useRoughness = 0, 1 do
 material:SetFloat("_UseRoughness", useRoughness)
 U.Graphics.Blit(metal, target, material)
 U.RenderTexture.active = target
 readout:ReadPixels(U.Rect(0, 0, 2, 2), 0, 0)
 local read = readout:GetPixel(0, 0)
 local expect = smooth:GetPixel(0, 0).r ^ 0.45
 if useRoughness == 1 then expect = 1 - expect end
 assert(math.abs(read.r - .25) < .015 and math.abs(read.g - .75) < .015 and read.b < .01)
 assert(math.abs(read.a - expect) < .015, tostring(read.a) .. ' != ' .. tostring(expect))
 end
end)
U.RenderTexture.active = active
for _, asset in ipairs({ material, metal, ao, smooth, readout, target }) do U.Object.DestroyImmediate(asset) end
assert(ok, failure)
return "SDK RGBA channels and roughness passed"
", "tutorial-mask", "null" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "SDK RGBA channels and roughness passed" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/DeleteAsset", "args": [ "Assets/TutorialMaskTest" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } } ] Use the output as the material's mask texture. The replay checked numeric values from the SDK shader with both roughness settings. Inspect the final appearance on the vehicle material.

manual/en/mod/mod-env-setup.html.title: Set Up the Modding Environment | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/mod-env-setup.html.summary: Set Up the Modding Environment 中文 | English Choose the route that matches your situation. The detailed steps live in the linked guides; this page is only the entry point. First-time install Download the named SDK ZIP from GitHub Releases, then verify its hash and extract it fully using the download reference. The release bundles the binary files, so Git is not required. Install the Unity version declared by the project and the modules for your target platform, following the version requirements. Follow project setup to open UnityProject in Unity Hub, keep the sibling Packages folder, and build a bundled template to verify the environment after import. Maintain the project with Git Follow the download and clone guide to install Git LFS, clone the repository, and complete git lfs pull. Open UnityProject with the version declared in the project's ProjectVersion.txt and finish importing as described in project setup. When updating the SDK, extract or check out into a new folder. Do not overwrite the new package with the old SDK's Packages folder; carry your own assets forward with the migration steps. Migrate an old project Move your assets together with their .meta files, mod packages, and build pipelines into the new SDK, preserving existing asset references and mod identifiers. Confirm references resolve step by step, then rebuild the linked objects and package to test. See the migration guide for the detailed rules. If your local GameHub build offers Create Project, you can also use the GameHub workflow.

manual/en/mod/mod-mirror-site-setup.html.title: Setting up a mod mirror site | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/mod-mirror-site-setup.html.summary: Setting up a mod mirror site 中文 | English A mirror publishes permitted workshop archives as a directly downloadable folder. It reduces load on the official downloader and still gives players the same packages when the official site is unstable. Keep archive integrity, platform ownership and filenames unchanged. History: the old JSON list The earlier setup used a public list as the mirror index: https://dl-workshop.windyverse.net/packages/files_list.json That JSON recorded mod names, update dates and download links, and the service refreshed it every 12 hours. A companion Python helper downloaded every mod from the list; it depended on requests and tqdm, tracked addresses in downloaded_files.json, and staged partial downloads in tmp. Those are descriptions of that period, not something to copy verbatim: today you can take the archives directly and treat the index as background only. A GET on that address returned HTTP 404 on 2026-11-18. Since then it describes the shape of the old approach rather than the source or authoritative list of mirror content. Archive only permitted workshop archives Publish only workshop archives you are allowed to redistribute. Keep each download as it is: do not rename or repack the archive, and do not copy packages from another platform to fill a folder. packages/ android/ win64/ ios/ Use one folder per platform and keep the original filename of each platform's .modpack build. Keep any matching .modpack.json so readers can check the platform, version, GUID, and content metadata. The full file manifest is in package.json inside the archive. Use NetDisk as a mirror With UC NetDisk as an example, let the client sync the packages folder to the cloud automatically. Share that folder only after synchronization finishes, and share it read-only so readers cannot delete or edit the source directory. Point the share at packages alone, not at temporary folders produced during the run. Static hosting alternative You can also serve the packages directory through Nginx or another static host. To preview the layout locally, run this command in the parent directory of packages: python -m http.server 8080 --bind 127.0.0.1 Open http://127.0.0.1:8080/packages/win64/, download a real file, and check the path and filename. Press Ctrl+C to stop the preview. Use the same folder layout on the public host and give readers read-only download links. Verify after synchronization Wait for synchronization or deployment to finish; do not publish the link mid-sync. Open the share as an ordinary reader and download a sample .modpack, confirming that no login or special permission is needed. In PowerShell run Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -LiteralPath "<file path>" separately on the source and downloaded copy. The hashes should match. If a .modpack.json exists, also check the platform, version, and GUID. Once verified, point players to Install mods so they can stage the package in the game's install queue. A mirror only serves installation packages, not development tools. The public SDK is a development project; see project download links for how to get it.

manual/en/mod/mod-texture-group.html.title: Legacy mod texture groups | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/mod-texture-group.html.summary: Legacy mod texture groups 中文 | English Older texture groups let players switch a vehicle to a named set of textures. The old example used a Cartoon group for the KV-2. The group name served as both the in-game label and the output folder. Each replacement texture kept the original file name and extension, including the extension on names such as KV_2_D. If you are maintaining an older project with this editor tool, create a CompressedPackageBuildPiplineData asset, set the group name, select Vehicle Custom Texture, add the replacements, and click Pack. Test the result in the matching game version and make sure the original textures can still be selected. The public SDK release sdk-2026.11.04.1 was checked for the old build asset type without finding it. For a new vehicle, bind your textures through its materials and vehicle data, then repack it with the vehicle tutorial. Check legacy texture group compatibility against the game version you intend to support.

The game requires AssetBundles built for the platform it runs on. Prerequisites Install the matching Unity version and platform modules. The project is registered in GameHub. If it is not, click Add Path in GameHub and point it at that Unity project. Local file: dependencies (adjacent UnityProject / Packages layout) resolve correctly, and the SDK dependency matches the build for this platform. Create the soft-linked project In GameHub, select the target platform you want to build for. GameHub creates a soft-linked project for that platform; click Copy to copy its path. Open Unity Hub, click Add project from disk, and enter the path copied in step 2. Click the version, change Current Platform to the platform of the project you created, make sure the name matches, then click Open. After the project opens, check the target in File → Build Settings and wait for import to finish. GameHub's linked projects share source assets. Each platform keeps its own Library. Follow the GameHub and Unity Hub steps manually, then use MCP to check the target of the open project. manual/en/mod/official-art-assets.html.summary: Official Art Assets 中文 | English Official production assets such as vehicles and maps live in the private repository WindyVerse/Panzer-War-Mods. The old GitLab community, sound, and map repositories are frozen and are kept for reference only. This page describes how authorized contributors work. Downloading and trying the SDK does not need repository access; see "Public SDK and official resources" below. Access Access to the official asset repository requires authorization. Send your GitHub account to the developers, have them grant repository access, and sign in to Git with the account that received the invitation. The public mod SDK needs no application; download it directly. Public SDK and official resources Download the public SDK from GitHub Releases and follow project setup to open UnityProject. For a Git checkout, use the download and clone guide. Public SDK releases The SDK and the official resources are two different repositories: the SDK is for setting up a project, testing, and packaging, while the official production resources are in the private repository. Being able to download from the SDK release page does not mean the official asset repository is public as well. Prepare the project Set up Git and Git LFS, see install Git, and add TortoiseGit if you prefer a graphical client. When you work on one package, use Git Bash in a clean checkout to fetch the package and its dependencies. This example uses Vehicles/German. GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1 git clone https://github.com/WindyVerse/Panzer-War-Mods.git cd Panzer-War-Mods python Tools/ci.py prepare Vehicles/German git lfs pull --include="<the lfs paths printed above>" prepare rewrites the package's project manifest. Before committing, use git diff -- Projects/Vehicles/Packages/manifest.json to confirm the only changes are from that command, then restore that one file. git restore -- Projects/Vehicles/Packages/manifest.json Open Projects/<Group> with Unity 2022.3.62f1, then edit and test-build locally as usual. Asset locations: one modpack corresponds to one local UPM package under Packages/<Group>/<Pack>, which holds the BuildPipeline and the resources unique to that package; assets shared by several packages go to Packages/<Group>/Shared. The SDK creation tools still generate new files into the project shell under Assets/Res/... and Assets/ModManager/. After creating them, drag those folders into the owning package in the Unity Project window; moving preserves their GUIDs. Personal editor settings such as the Steam game path live in Assets/EditorStorage.json, which is not committed. When the file is absent, start from Projects/<Group>/EditorStorage.template.json. Keep existing paths and .meta files when moving or re-exporting assets so GUIDs and references survive. Naming and export requirements are in art asset naming and upload standards. Make one coherent change Keep one related change per branch so the developers can review and merge it. Do not mix unrelated cleanup, formatting, or re-exports into the same branch. A local test build rewrites the build records in the ModPackage asset (file list, createdTime). If you only tested a build locally, do not commit those changes. Create a branch, commit, and push The full command-line flow: git switch main git pull git switch -c <topic>-mod git status git add <the files you changed> git commit -m "<what you changed>" git push -u origin <topic>-mod Then open a pull request from that branch to main on GitHub and state which package you changed, what you changed, and how you verified it. With TortoiseGit, do the same steps from the context menu of the project folder: TortoiseGit → Create branch to create the branch. Name it <topic>-mod, for example the tank you changed and what you changed on it. Switch to that branch before making your edits. Right-click TortoiseGit → Commit. In the commit dialog, tick only the files you changed. If a file is not yours, leave it unticked instead of adding everything. Right-click TortoiseGit → Push, confirm the branch name, push, and then open the pull request on GitHub. You can keep adding commits to your branch. Including only your own files in the commit is what keeps other people's uncommitted work in the same working tree out of it. Verification Run the static check before committing. It fills in undeclared package dependencies and reports the remaining problems: python Tools/check.py --fix If you changed package contents, build and verify the current platform locally through the same entry CI uses. The artifact lands in Artifacts/local/: python Tools/ci.py build Vehicles/German Once that passes, run Build modpack in the mod repository's GitHub Actions, fill in the affected packs and target platform, and set publish=none for a verification build. The workflow trims dependencies, pulls the matching LFS content, builds, and verifies. See continuous mod builds for the flow and artifact checks, and multi-platform build for platform differences. After downloading the artifact, check the target platform, GUID, modVersion, manifest files, and the .modpack.json sidecar with the same name, then load the initial vehicles, maps, sounds, materials, and config in the game on that platform. A successful CI build only means the artifact passed its checks; it does not mean it has run in the actual game. Publishing to the workshop is a separate flow: publish=sandbox publishes a test build, and publish=production is allowed only from main. Increment modVersion first when the contents of an already published package change. Update after merge Once your branch is merged into main, switch back to main and pull the latest project, which now contains your changes and everyone else's: git switch main git pull For further work, create a new branch from the updated main. If the pull fails, stash only your own changes, pull, then restore them: git stash push -m "uncommitted work on my branch" -- <your files> git pull git stash pop Stash only your files so other people's work in the same tree is not swept in. Run git status again afterwards and confirm nothing is left with conflict markers. When an asset shows as Missing, record the exact path or GUID and report it to the developers; do not delete or recreate the asset yourself. Report missing paths from check.py the same way. Historical material The following comes from the older page. Interface wording, repository addresses, and screenshots may differ from the current version; treat the text above as authoritative. Old GitLab repositories (the map ones had to sit under the same parent directory as the community repository): Community repository: https://lab.windyverse.net/modder/panzer-war-community-mods Sound repository: https://lab.windyverse.net/modder/Panzer-War-Fmod Map repository: https://lab.windyverse.net/modder/ShanghaiWindyMaps Public resources: https://lab.windyverse.net/modder/ShanghaiWindyPublicResources Older video tutorials (recorded against the old interface, background only): Downloading, using, and contributing to the mod project (Chinese) Writing custom scripts and tuning vehicle values in the mod project (Chinese) The older page described "the main project files under Assets/Res/Vehicles/Ground/Data" with screenshots; that path refers to assets in the project shell, while package assets now live under Packages/<Group>/<Pack>. The older in-editor Git workflow of creating a branch, committing, and pulling matches the TortoiseGit steps above.

manual/en/mod/physics-wheels.html.summary: Configure a Wheeled Vehicle 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run physics-wheels --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "vehicle": "${fixture}/Tutorial_WheeledVehicle.asset", "model": "${fixture}/Tutorial_WheeledBody.prefab", "collider": "${fixture}/Tutorial_WheelCollider.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } Current vehicles use the wheeled mode of TrackController. The old guide used NPhysicCarController, Rigidbody, CenterOfMass, and NPhysic on the hull root, with WheelController and a friction preset on each wheel. These names help identify an older setup during migration. The current mode and wheel settings use PTCParameter and the collider templates below. 1. Prepare the hull and wheel nodes Start from the vehicle setup guide. Under the visual model root, create Wheels with FrontLeft, FrontRight, RearLeft, and RearRight as its children. Check the wheel origins from the side and front and make sure they are centered on their axles. In the cooked prefab, the builder creates VehicleDynamics as a sibling of Wheels. The builder uses an existing Rigidbody on the model root or creates one from the vehicle parameters. To adjust the center of gravity, open VehicleData → Edit, move the orange Center Of Gravity node, and press K in Scene view to save it. The picture shows the finished Mobility configuration. TankWheelCollider supplies the tire collider parameters and isWheelVehicle enables wheeled mode. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${model}", "mode": "create", "component": "UnityEngine.Rigidbody", "children": [ "VehicleDynamics", "Wheels/FrontLeft", "Wheels/FrontRight", "Wheels/RearLeft", "Wheels/RearRight" ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/PatriotRadar/BuiltIn-Patriot-Radar_VehicleTextData.asset", "${vehicle}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/isStationary", "value": "false" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 2. Group wheels by drive and steering Open the Mobility tab of VehicleTextData and expand PTCParameter. Assign a template prefab with a Unity WheelCollider to TankWheelCollider. The runtime wheels copy its radius, suspension and friction settings. A group can override this with steerData.wheelCollider. An empty group template falls back to the main template. Add two entries to steerableWheels. All wheels paths are resolved relative to the parent of VehicleDynamics. Group Paths isMotor isSteerable maxSteerAngle Front Wheels/FrontLeft, Wheels/FrontRight true true 28° Rear Wheels/RearLeft, Wheels/RearRight true false 0° Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/PatriotRadar/BuiltIn-Patriot-Radar_WheelCollider.prefab", "${collider}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/PTCParameter/TankWheelCollider", "value": "@asset:${collider}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/PTCParameter/steerableWheels", "value": "[{\"wheels\": [\"Wheels/FrontLeft\", \"Wheels/FrontRight\"], \"steerData\": {\"isMotor\": true, \"isSteerable\": true, \"maxSteerAngle\": 28}}, {\"wheels\": [\"Wheels/RearLeft\", \"Wheels/RearRight\"], \"steerData\": {\"isMotor\": true, \"isSteerable\": false, \"maxSteerAngle\": 0}}]" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 3. Enable wheeled mode Enable isWheelVehicle in the same Mobility tab. This example uses no track data, so TrackData stays empty. Keep Stationary Base off so the ordinary ground vehicle uses TrackController. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/PTCParameter/isWheelVehicle", "value": "true" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/PTCParameter/TrackData", "value": "null" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 4. Save and check Save the hull and configuration, then pack again. Check that each configured path points to one axle node. Drive on flat ground in the Vehicle Playground to check tire contact, front-wheel steering, and rear-wheel alignment, then try a slope. Check model axes and steering groups if a wheel faces the wrong way. Check the group's actual collider template if the tires lose grip unexpectedly.
