manual/en/mod/project-download-links.htm.title: Project download reference | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/project-download-links.htm.summary: Project download reference 中文 | English 1. Get the release package Open the Panzer War Mod SDK releases, expand Assets, and download Panzer-War-Mod-SDK-sdk-*.zip (public release sdk-2026.11.04.1 is about 600 MB). The same release's Assets include SHA256SUMS.txt and release.json; download both. release.json records that release's Unity information in a field named sdk.unity; the editor version string m_EditorVersion is not in release.json but in UnityProject/ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt after extraction. Do not use the auto-generated Source code (zip) / Source code (tar.gz) archives; they may contain only Git LFS pointers. Follow project setup to extract and open the project, or create a project through GameHub if it offers Create Project. 2. Verify the download on Windows In PowerShell, change to your download folder and replace the file name with the one you actually downloaded: Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 .\Panzer-War-Mod-SDK-sdk-2026.11.04.1.zip Compare the printed Hash character by character with the entry for the same file name in SHA256SUMS.txt, ignoring case: PowerShell prints uppercase hex while the list may be lowercase or mixed case, so hexadecimal digests must be compared case-insensitively. Extract only when they match. A different file name means you compared the wrong line; a different hash means the download is corrupt or incomplete, or you fetched the wrong file or release, so check the file name and version and download it again. On macOS: shasum -a 256 Panzer-War-Mod-SDK-sdk-2026.11.04.1.zip On Linux: sha256sum Panzer-War-Mod-SDK-sdk-2026.11.04.1.zip 3. Release ZIP versus Git and LFS Use the release ZIP (recommended): extract the whole archive, keep UnityProject next to Packages, and open UnityProject in Unity. The release bundles the real DLLs and local dependencies, so no Git or LFS install and no git lfs pull is needed. Use a Git clone: for readers who want to track repository updates or history. Install Git LFS and finish the pull before opening the project: git lfs install git clone https://github.com/WindyVerse/Panzer-War-Mod-SDK.git cd Panzer-War-Mod-SDK git lfs pull If LFS has not finished, or you downloaded a source archive, binary files become pointer files. If a DLL opens as a few lines of text whose first line is version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1, it is an LFS pointer rather than a real binary: for a Git checkout run git lfs pull again, and for a ZIP download use the named release ZIP instead of Source code. Pointer files cause Unity plugin-loading or DLL errors. The SDK is the public modding package. Official vehicles, maps and other assets live in the separate private Panzer-War-Mods repository, and the game itself is built from Panzer-War-Client. Use the SDK unless you are changing official assets or client code.

manual/en/mod/reactive-armor.html.title: Configure reactive armor | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/reactive-armor.html.summary: Configure reactive armor 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. Enable Dev Mode Turn on Dev Mode in the editor. The build pipeline inspector then shows the Export Shader Variants button; it is hidden in normal mode. Create the shader collection Create a Shader Collection (ShaderCollectionData) asset and assign it to the pipeline field Shader Variant Collections (shaderCollectionData). This asset only describes what to collect. Add shader keywords In Shader Keywords, add the source shader and the feature keywords for that shader. Keywords must exist in the shader itself — for example _FOG_LINEAR, _FOG_EXP, _FOG_EXP2 are valid only when the shader declares them. Check the actual keyword names instead of guessing. Export the variants Press Export Shader Variants. The tool writes a .shadervariants file beside the pipeline's build .asset, built from the pipeline dependency paths. Register the generated collection Add the generated Unity ShaderVariantCollection to Linked Objects. The settings asset above is its input. Enable both Load Manifest Dependence and Share Dependence Shader on the build pipeline. The collector checks both settings. Build and test Build for the target platform, then install the result and check fog and material variants in game. Share the shader bundle instead of merging shader source into the .shader file. Regenerate after shader changes Re-export the variants whenever the shader or its keywords change, then rebuild the modpack. The sample creates one variant using the vehicle shader's declared _KEYWORD_ENABLE_CAMO keyword. It verifies the input and output asset bindings and enables shader sharing on the build pipeline. manual/en/mod/spg-td-hydraulic-suspensio.summary: Configure SPG, tank destroyer, and Strv hydraulic suspension actions 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run spg-td-hydraulic-suspension --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "vehicle": "${fixture}/Tutorial_TurretVehicle.asset", "shared": "${fixture}/Tutorial_SharedTurret.asset", "spg": "${fixture}/Tutorial_SPG.asset", "td": "${fixture}/Tutorial_TD.asset", "strv": "${fixture}/Tutorial_Hydraulic.asset" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } Choose a turret action for the main turret in VehicleTextData. This example uses separate tutorial assets to demonstrate TD, SPG, and Strv configurations and how SharedTurretData takes precedence. 1. Create the turret action assets In the Project window, choose Create > A Panzer War - 装甲纷争 > G Ground Vehicle - 地面载具 > Turret Action - 炮塔逻辑. Create TD - 反坦, SPG - 火炮, and Hydraulic - 液压 assets named Tutorial_TD, Tutorial_SPG, and Tutorial_Hydraulic. A turret parameter has one actionData slot. The TD asset enables hull steering assistance and has no extra settings. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateAsset", "args": [ "@static:UnityEngine.ScriptableObject/CreateInstance(ShanghaiWindy.Core.SPGTurretAction)", "${spg}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateAsset", "args": [ "@static:UnityEngine.ScriptableObject/CreateInstance(ShanghaiWindy.Core.TDTurretAction)", "${td}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateAsset", "args": [ "@static:UnityEngine.ScriptableObject/CreateInstance(ShanghaiWindy.Core.StrvTurretAction)", "${strv}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 2. Set the SPG aiming parameter Select Tutorial_SPG and set maxDistance to 450. The value is used when updating the overhead camera and calculating the fallback trajectory preview duration for an unreachable target. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${spg}/maxDistance", "value": "450" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 3. Set the Strv hydraulic parameters Select Tutorial_Hydraulic. Keep the three attack-mode speed modifiers at their defaults and set the suspension and automatic control fields below. Field Value attackingSuspension 0.5 wheelElevateClamp 0.45 maxElevateAnglePerSecond 0.1 autoPidFactors (3, 0, 2.5) Unity takes the absolute value of the first three fields during asset validation and caps wheelElevateClamp at attackingSuspension. The hydraulic action requires a tracked chassis with TrackController and working road wheels. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${strv}/attackingSuspension", "value": "0.5" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${strv}/wheelElevateClamp", "value": "0.45" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${strv}/maxElevateAnglePerSecond", "value": "0.1" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${strv}/autoPidFactors", "value": "3,0,2.5" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 4. Assign the main turret action Open a copy of VehicleTextData. Clear sharedTurretData and assign Tutorial_TD to MTParameter.actionData, then switch it to Tutorial_SPG. To reuse a turret configuration, open a copy of SharedTurretData, set turretParameter.actionData to Tutorial_Hydraulic, and assign the shared asset to the vehicle's sharedTurretData. The main turret takes its parameters from the shared asset when one is assigned. The Inspector then hides the local MTParameter. Each simple fire-control system reads its own turret parameters. manual/en/mod/tank-active-protection.htm.title: Tank active protection system | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/tank-active-protection.htm.summary: Tank active protection system 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run tank-active-protection --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "aps": "${fixture}/Tutorial_ApsPart.asset", "native": "${fixture}/Tutorial_NativeAps.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/DIY/Function/Aps/Aps.asset", "${aps}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } } ] } This tutorial covers the APS data entry point, how coverage is evaluated, and how to validate one interception setup in the editor. 1. Attach the APS component Find the visual model using the first-tank guide and open it in Prefab Mode, pick the hull or a suitable mount child under it in the Hierarchy, then use Inspector > Add Component > Vehicle Aps Attachment Mono Component (C# type VehicleApsAttachmentMonoComponent). On the same node, check that VehicleAttachmentMonoComponent uses Specific and points to the APS component. Expand apsAttachmentSlot, then configure the APS Profile. The screenshot example assigns the ApsMount transform under the hull as the mount point and binds at least one FirePoint in Fire Points. The blue Z arrow sets forward; when no transform is assigned, the vehicle's own rotation is used for coverage. The Visual Profile controls audiovisual feedback, and the Turret Profile is optional, needed only when the launcher rotates. The built-in DIY example lives at Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/DIY/Function/Aps/Aps.asset and is a DIYApsData; its visual prefab supplies the ApsTurret and ApsTurret/ApsGun paths, and presets may override the base DIY profile. That prefab stores the graphics hierarchy, while the screenshot shows the component configuration. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${native}", "mode": "create", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleApsAttachmentMonoComponent", "children": [ "ApsMount", "ApsMount/FirePoint" ], "values": { "apsAttachmentSlot": { "attachment": { "apsProfile": { "coverageAngle": 270, "ammoCount": 4, "cooldown": 1.5 }, "firePoints": [ null ] } } }, "references": [ { "property": "apsAttachmentSlot.attachment.mountTransform", "child": "ApsMount" }, { "property": "apsAttachmentSlot.attachment.firePoints.Array.data[0]", "child": "ApsMount/FirePoint", "component": "UnityEngine.GameObject" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${native}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleAttachmentMonoComponent", "values": { "attachmentSlotType": 1 }, "references": [ { "property": "specificAttachmentMonoComponent", "child": "", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleApsAttachmentMonoComponent" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${aps}/turretPath" }, "expect": { "contains": "ApsTurret" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${aps}/gunPath" }, "expect": { "contains": "ApsTurret/ApsGun" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${native}/VehicleApsAttachmentMonoComponent/apsAttachmentSlot/attachment/firePoints/0/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "FirePoint" } } ] 2. Understand coverage and interception conditions The screenshot depicts the native VehicleApsAttachmentMonoComponent configured with an ApsMount and a FirePoint, 4 charges, a 1.5 s cooldown, and 270 degrees of coverage. These are the teaching values. detectionRadius is the threat detection distance, fireRadius is where a tracked closing projectile can trigger an interception, and minInterceptRadius is the smallest qualifying distance. The 80 m, 40 m, and 8 m figures, along with 0.95 for interceptProbability, are APSProfile source defaults. Coverage is evaluated relative to the mounted forward direction. With no useTraverseLimits, coverage is a 3D cone; with it enabled, the check uses local yaw within half the coverage angle plus up/down elevation limits. HardKill uses interception and fires, while the other scanning branch detects without firing. Warhead mass and chance relate to whether an interception succeeds, not to detection. Cooldown and remaining charges likewise limit consecutive interceptions. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${native}/VehicleApsAttachmentMonoComponent/apsAttachmentSlot/attachment/apsProfile/coverageAngle" }, "expect": { "contains": "270" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${aps}/apsProfile" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${aps}/presets" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${aps}/launcherParameter/maxTurretAngle" } } ] 3. Test the APS setup APS is enabled in the Editor. Packaged builds also check runtime feature availability. First open the visual model in Prefab Mode and check that apsAttachmentSlot, the APS Profile, ApsMount, and Fire Points point at the right nodes. Save, rebuild and enter the test range. Try a compatible incoming game projectile from within the mounted coverage, then watch whether it is intercepted and whether the status display and charge use match expectations. Repeat the shot from outside coverage and confirm nothing is intercepted. Run out of charges, fire once more, and confirm no further interception happens. Diagnosis: if nothing triggers, confirm the APS runtime feature is enabled in the Editor, then check coverage angle, elevation limits, the warhead allowlist, and the speed and mass thresholds. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run tank-engine-rpm --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "text": "${fixture}/Tutorial_EngineVehicleText.asset", "fmod": "${fixture}/Tutorial_EngineSound.asset" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/Editor/DocumentationSamples/vehicle-basics/Tutorial_NativeText.asset", "${text}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/FMod/Tank/Engine/kv220.asset", "${fmod}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } } ] } Once your first vehicle can move forward and reverse, tune its engine, shifts and sound. Take a baseline speed and RPM reading on level ground, then change one group of settings at a time. 1. Find the vehicle's engine parameters Select VehicleTextData in Project and open Mobility → Track Params (PTCParameter). Check Mass, the wheel collider prefab and the track reference. The teaching tank has a mass of 30,000 kg. Check Shared Engine Data (sharedEngineData). With an empty reference, edit the local parameters. With a reference assigned, open SharedEngineData to edit the shared engine and sound. To tune a single vehicle, duplicate that asset and assign the copy. Set the power and speed limits. The example uses engineTorque = 3500, maxSpeed = 35 km/h and minSpeed = 10 km/h. Enter the reverse limit, minSpeed, as a positive magnitude. Parameter How to tune it engineTorque, reversingEngineTorque Base drive torque for the forward and reverse directions. For a weak launch, check the wheel colliders and mass first, then increase torque in steps. engineTorqueCurve Speed in km/h on the horizontal axis and drive output multiplier on the vertical axis. The low-speed keys affect launch. If output falls to zero too early, the tank may never reach the configured speed. enableReverseEngineTorqueCurve Enable it to edit a separate reverseEngineTorqueCurve. brakeTorque, steerTorque Tune braking and steering separately. Accelerate in a straight line before checking braking and low-speed turns. maxSpeed, minSpeed Forward and reverse speed caps. Achievable speed also depends on power, terrain and resistance. Generate gears and set the RPM range Expand Gear, set Total Gears to 5 and click the Gear initialization button (InitGear()). It enables gears and rebuilds the list. Tracked vehicles use the tracked drivetrain. Enable Gear also exposes these authoring fields. Save a copy before overwriting a custom gear table. Verify that the RPM Ratio values in gears are positive and decrease from one gear to the next. The tracked drivetrain uses their relative spacing. It derives the final drive from the speed cap and torque curve. The wheeled-drive fields finalRatio and targetSpeedForNextGear do not enter that calculation. Set minEngineRPM = 600, gearShiftDownRPM = 800, gearShiftUpRPM = 1300 and maxEngineRPM = 1500. Keep idle, downshift, upshift and redline in ascending RPM order. The tracked drivetrain adjusts actual shift points for throttle and load. Compare the shift delay and rev rise when tuning gearShiftingDelay and engineInertia. Assign a working VehicleEngineFmodSoundData to Engine Sound (vehicleEngineFmodSoundData). The vehicle reports physical revs per minute. FMOD's running event receives a normalized 0–100 RPM value between idle and redline. Read both values with the TankAPI engine state. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run tank-fire-settings --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "text": "${fixture}/Tutorial_FireVehicleText.asset", "shared": "${fixture}/Tutorial_FireSharedGun.asset", "bullet": "${fixture}/Tutorial_FireAP.asset" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/Editor/DocumentationSamples/vehicle-basics/Tutorial_NativeText.asset", "${text}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/PatriotRadar/BuiltIn-Patriot-Radar-SharedGun.asset", "${shared}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/Editor/DocumentationSamples/vehicle-basics/Tutorial-76mm-AP.asset", "${bullet}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } } ] } Once your first tank can drive, configure its main gun and firing effects. See ammunition and effects for projectile flight, penetration and impact effects. 1. Find the gun data the vehicle uses Select the vehicle's VehicleTextData in Project and open the Fire tab. Check Shared Gun Data (sharedGunData). With an empty reference, edit the local Tank Fire Params (TFParameter). If a SharedGunData asset is assigned, open that asset and expand its tankFireParameter. The game reads the shared asset first. To tune one vehicle, duplicate the asset and assign the copy to that vehicle. Click + in Bullet Data (bulletData) and drag the first test round into slot 0. Assign an existing sound asset to Bullet Sound (fmodBulletSound) and select Muzzle Middle for Muzzle Fire (muzzleFire). Check FFPoint and EffectStart in the model. Position them at the muzzle and point their local +Z down the line of fire. Use the first-tank model setup as a reference, then check each secondary turret's own firing points. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/sharedGunData", "value": "null" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/TFParameter/bulletData/0", "value": "@asset:${bullet}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/TFParameter/bulletData/0/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "Tutorial_FireAP" } } ] 2. Set the reload mode and dispersion Set Fire State (fireState) to Standard, Reload Time (ReloadTime) to 6 seconds and Ammo Count (AmmoCount) to 30 rounds. Ammo Count configures the gun's reserve. If you switch modes, fill in the timing fields for the new mode. Fire State Parameters to configure Standard ReloadTime sets the standard reload time in seconds. hasSlot shows Slot Count and Slot Duration for weapons with a burst window. Advance SmallReloadTime, LargeReloadTime, and MaxSmallAmmo set the short reload in seconds, the long reload in seconds, and the number of rounds per magazine. Try 2 seconds, 33 seconds, and 4 rounds. Drum drumFire.fireDuration controls shot spacing. Enter times for each replenishment stage in drumFire.reloadTime. Start with the same times to observe individual rounds replenishing before tuning each stage. Energy Under energyFire, configure the energy per shot (perShotEnergy), capacity (totalEnergy), shot interval (perShotInterval), and effect duration (vfxDuration). The Dispersion area has two sets of controls. The outer dispersion field governs fixed spread, with a standard deviation at 100 m of 100 times that value. Expand Spread (fireSpread) for the shrinking reticle mode. The example sets aimTime to 2 seconds and dispersion to 0.35. A larger aimTime slows convergence. A positive value also marks the spread profile as configured. moveSpreadCoff, traverseSpreadCoff, gunSpreadCoff, afterFiredCoff, and damagedCoff control the effect of motion, hull traverse, gun motion, firing, and damage. Keep the working sample coefficients for the first test, then tune them one at a time. See fixed-angle reload to return the gun to a set angle during reloading. manual/en/mod/tank-light-settings.html.summary: Tank Light Settings 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run tank-light-settings --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "light": "${fixture}/Tutorial_ArrayLights.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/Light/AuthoringSamples/Array4.prefab", "${light}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } } ] } This guide is for players who already have a working tank and want to install lights, configure beams and light types in Unity, then verify the result in game. 1. Attach lights with CustomShape Under MainBody, create a separate child node for the left light and another for the right light. Each light root needs VehicleLightAttachmentMonoComponent, plus VehicleAttachmentMonoComponent with attachmentSlotType set to Specific and specificAttachmentMonoComponent pointing at the former. The custom editor adds the companion component while drawing the light node, so confirm the link exists before you save. Next, configure the slot data. Assign the light mount transform in lightAttachmentSlot.attachment.lightTransform (灯光位置 / Light Transform). For multi-lens lights you can start from our Array4 sample as a teaching reference, or create separate LensSurface children under lightTransform, each using MeshFilter and MeshRenderer with the lamp material. See the light component guide for presets, duplication and mirroring. Then set lightSizeType (灯光大小类型 / Light Size Type) to CustomShape. Circle and HalfCircle use radiusSize, RectSmall, RectMiddle and RectLarge use rectSize, and CustomShape uses customShapeRenderers. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${light}/GetComponent(ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleAttachmentMonoComponent)/attachmentSlotType" }, "expect": { "contains": "Specific" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${light}/GetComponent(ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleLightAttachmentMonoComponent)/lightAttachmentSlot/attachment/lightSizeType" }, "expect": { "contains": "CustomShape" } } ] 2. Aim the light and set the type The Array4 sample uses four lens renderers, four emitter transforms and one beam origin. lensEmitters carries the label 发光点（留空沿用旧配置） / Emitters (empty uses legacy placement). Use up to eight unique child transforms under lightTransform, keep glareScale and glareWeight finite and non-negative with a positive total weight, and give each lens one material and one submesh when you fill emitters explicitly. Place emitters at the lamp faces and use local +Z as the forward direction. beamOrigin carries the label 光束节点（+Z 为最终出光方向） / Beam origin (+Z is the final beam direction). It is an optional child node, so orient the arrows in Scene View to confirm the final beam direction. Set lightType (灯光类型 / Light Type) to LowBeam, HighBeam, PositionLight, BrakeLight, ReverseLight, LeftBlinker or RightBlinker. Fill colors with Set From Preset when the interface offers it, and keep baseColor and emissionColor separate. isBlinker exposes a frequency and an on fraction, so frequency 1 with fraction 0.5 produces half a second on per second. CustomShape offers a preview for lights on and off. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${light}/GetComponent(ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleLightAttachmentMonoComponent)/lightAttachmentSlot/attachment/beamOrigin" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${light}/GetComponent(ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleLightAttachmentMonoComponent)/lightAttachmentSlot/attachment/lensEmitters" } } ] 3. Test and diagnose Save and repack the mod, then drive in a dim test scene and compare switchable beams, brake and reverse lights, and the indicators using the assigned controls. If a lens glows but the beam points the wrong way, check the local +Z direction of beamOrigin. If no light appears, check the slot, renderer, material and child references in the actual mod prefab before you adjust HDR. This workflow has two stages: the editor recipe checks the asset wiring, and a player session verifies runtime behavior. manual/en/mod/tank-radar-settings.html.summary: Tank Radar Settings 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run tank-radar-settings --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "text": "${fixture}/Tutorial_RadarVehicleText.asset" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/PatriotRadar/BuiltIn-Patriot-Radar_VehicleTextData.asset", "${text}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } } ] } This guide is for players who already have a working tank and want to enable the AA radar in vehicle text data, tune scan parameters, and check detection and lock behavior in game. 1. Enable the radar Select the tank's assigned VehicleTextData, open Misc → AA Radar, expand AA Radar Data (groundAARadarData), and turn on Has Radar (hasRadar). That field defaults to false. The vehicle loads the ground scan from this data and takes its aim frame from the turret transform, with the hull as a fallback. For a separate decorative rotating antenna, add VehicleRadarAttachment in the Universal slot. It rotates radarTransform along a local axis at rotateSpeed in degrees per second, and it stays independent from the functional radar. The ground setting is also independent of aircraft radar and of Lua display integrations. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/groundAARadarData/hasRadar", "value": "true" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/groundAARadarData/hasRadar" }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } } ] 2. Tune the scan The table below lists units and defaults, or describes how the field behaves. Field Unit or default Notes maxDetectionRange metres, default 15000 Reference range for a target with a radar cross-section of 5 m² searchAzimuthHalfAngle degrees, default 45 Azimuth search half angle searchElevationHalfAngle degrees, default 30 Elevation search half angle scanRate degrees per second, default 60 Scan rate in directional mode isFullRotation default false Whether the scan runs full rotation fullRotationRate degrees per second, default 60 Full rotation rate, about 6 seconds per turn, applies to SRC and TWS, keep the rate positive minElevationAngle degrees, default 2 Minimum elevation detectGroundTargets default false Bypasses elevation clutter rejection and still respects coverage and range limits displayRanges metres, defaults 2500/5000/10000/20000 Display scale steps canUsePD default true Whether PD mode is available canUseTWS default true Whether TWS mode is available pdMinDetectableSpeed metres per second, default 30 Radial speed threshold twsMaxTracks default 4 TWS simultaneous track limit acmScanHalfAngle and acmMaxRange 15 degrees, 8000 m Air combat maneuver mode envelope trackConeHalfAngle 30 degrees Track mode envelope lockAcquireTime seconds, default 0.5 Lock acquisition time The Patriot asset shows maxDetectionRange as 16000, so treat that number as a sample value and read its other fields from the asset itself. Enable hasIRST for infrared search. Its irstDetectionRange defaults to 10,000 m. You can also set chaff count, duration and cooldown, along with ECCM, IFF, and target type recognition (NCTR). The decorative antenna speed controls the model. scanRate controls how fast the functional scan sweeps the sector. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/groundAARadarData/maxDetectionRange", "value": "16000" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/groundAARadarData/maxDetectionRange" }, "expect": { "contains": "16000" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/groundAARadarData/searchAzimuthHalfAngle", "value": "45" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/groundAARadarData/searchAzimuthHalfAngle" }, "expect": { "contains": "45" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/groundAARadarData/searchElevationHalfAngle", "value": "30" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/groundAARadarData/searchElevationHalfAngle" }, "expect": { "contains": "30" } } ] 3. Runtime check Repack the mod and possess the vehicle locally. Turn on the radar with the configured controls, bring an aircraft into the scan area, and compare target range and bearing, the lock, the range scale, and either the sector pointing or a single sweep while full rotation is allowed. If ground target detection is enabled, compare a ground target as well. To drive a model from the actual scan, use GetScanAzimuth as described in the RadarAPI display guide. Figures and values in the editor verify field references and values, and detection and lock behavior require a game session. When troubleshooting, check the enable flag and asset link, the assigned control action, the turret frame, and the mode and clutter settings in that order. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/groundAARadarData/maxDetectionRange" }, "expect": { "contains": "16000" } } ] Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Runtime test pending. Bind the vehicle entity ID and its VehicleInitSystem index. Read the work mode, switch it, and observe the scan azimuth. Use an eligible target for detection and lock testing. manual/en/mod/tank-shell-ejection-animat.title: Create a tank shell ejection animation | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/tank-shell-ejection-animat.summary: Create a tank shell ejection animation 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run tank-shell-ejection-animation --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "rig": "${fixture}/Tutorial_ShellRig.fbx", "model": "${fixture}/Tutorial_ShellRig.prefab", "clip": "${fixture}/Tutorial_ShellEject.anim", "script": "${fixture}/PlayAnimationComponent.lua" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } Adapted from 樱花's original tank shell ejection tutorial. Build the casing and ejection mechanism under the turret in Blender, author the clip in Unity, then bind playback to the firing event in Lua. 1. Prepare and import the model In Blender, place the casing inside the turret and parent it to the turret. The example names the casing Casing. Set the ejection mechanism's pivot at its center of rotation. If the rotation axis differs from the global axes, add an empty, orient it to the local axis, and parent the mechanism to it. The example calls this empty MechanismPivot. Export an FBX and import it into Unity. Confirm that it contains Turret/Casing and Turret/MechanismPivot, then create a prefab for the setup. The recipe builds and exports the sample using Blender in background mode. If Unity cannot find Blender, set BLENDER to its executable before starting the editor. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Editor.ShellEjectionAuthoring/ExportRig", "args": [ "${fixture}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "Tutorial_ShellRig.fbx" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Editor.ShellEjectionAuthoring/EnsureRigPrefab", "args": [ "${rig}", "${model}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/Turret/Casing/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "(String) Casing" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/Turret/MechanismPivot/Mechanism/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "(String) Mechanism" } } ] 2. Author and assign the animation Select the prefab root in Unity's Animation window and create Tutorial_ShellEject.anim. Add three keyframes to the casing's local Position for rest, ejection and return. The example moves the casing 0.35 units on local X at 0.2 seconds and returns it to its start at 0.4 seconds. The local Rotation curves on MechanismPivot open the mechanism by 35° at 0.2 seconds and then return it to rest. Set the clip to Legacy and leave its Wrap Mode at Default. Add Animation to the root, assign the default clip and turn off Play Automatically so Lua can start it. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Editor.ShellEjectionAuthoring/WriteClip", "args": [ "${fixture}", "${model}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "Turret/Casing/m_LocalPosition.x: 3 keys" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Editor.ShellEjectionAuthoring/AssignClip", "args": [ "${model}", "${clip}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "Tutorial_ShellEject" } } ] 3. Bind the firing event Add LuaBehaviorMono to the same root. Save this script as PlayAnimationComponent.lua and assign it to Behavior. The script registers for the first fire system after the vehicle loads. For a vehicle with multiple guns, use the index of the intended system in the fire list. Behavior() Property = {} local PlayAnimationComponent = class("PlayAnimationComponent") function PlayAnimationComponent:OnStarted() local animation = self.script:GetNativeComponent("Animation") local found, vehicle = self.script:TryGetTankInitSystem() if not animation or not found then return end VehicleAPI.RegisterVehicleLoadedEvent(vehicle, function() VehicleAPI.RegisterBulletFiredEvent(vehicle, 0, function() animation:Play() end) end) end return PlayAnimationComponent Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Editor.ShellEjectionAuthoring/ImportBehavior", "args": [ "${fixture}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "PlayAnimationComponent.lua" } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${model}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.Lua.LuaBehaviorMono", "references": [ { "property": "luaBehavior", "asset": "${script}", "type": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.Lua.LuaBehaviorScript" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 4. Save and verify Save the prefab and confirm that Animation and LuaBehaviorMono are on the same node. Check the default clip, its Legacy setting and the Lua reference. The recipe reads back the position and rotation curves. Fire the assembled vehicle in game to check the callback and playback. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${clip}/legacy" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${clip}/wrapMode" }, "expect": { "contains": "Default" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/Animation/clip/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "Tutorial_ShellEject" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/Animation/playAutomatically" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) False" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/LuaBehaviorMono/luaBehavior/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "PlayAnimationComponent" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/LuaBehaviorMono/luaBehavior/lua" }, "expect": { "contains": "RegisterBulletFiredEvent" } } ]

manual/en/mod/tank-turret-settings.html.title: Tank turret traverse, elevation and stabilizers | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/tank-turret-settings.html.summary: Tank turret traverse, elevation and stabilizers 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run tank-turret-settings --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "text": "${fixture}/Tutorial_TurretVehicleText.asset", "model": "${fixture}/Tutorial_TurretModel.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/Editor/DocumentationSamples/vehicle-basics/Tutorial_NativeText.asset", "${text}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/Editor/DocumentationSamples/vehicle-basics/Tutorial_NativePackModel.prefab", "${model}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } } ] } Start with the main gun model from the first-tank guide. Set up the turret and gun pivots first, then configure traverse, elevation and stabilizers. 1. Set up the main gun hierarchy Create Turret → Gun → Dym below the visual model root. Parent the turret mesh to Turret and the recoiling barrel mesh to Dym. Put the turret pivot on the turret ring and the Gun pivot at the elevation axis. Dym moves with recoil. Check model axes, with local +Z forward and +Y up. Place FFPoint, EffectStart and the gunner camera reference as in the main model setup. Rotate and elevate the model by hand to check that the muzzle and reference points follow their intended parts. Inspect the generated prefab. The assembler names the runtime nodes TurretTransform, GunTransform, and GunDym. Keep Turret/Gun/Dym in the source model for the next build. Bind secondary turrets separately using the multi-turret data. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/Turret/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "Turret" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/Turret/Gun/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "Gun" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/Turret/Gun/Dym/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "Dym" } } ] 2. Set traverse, stabilization and limits Open the Turret tab of VehicleTextData. With no Shared Turret Data (sharedTurretData) assigned, edit Turret Params (MTParameter). With a shared asset assigned, open it and edit turretParameter. Duplicate the shared asset first to tune one vehicle. Field Teaching values and purpose maxTurretAngle 180° allows 180° on either side. A value of 45° allows 45° on either side. isNonSymmetricTurret Enables separate maxTurretNegativeAngle and maxTurretPositiveAngle, for example −30° and +45°. UpMaxDegree, DownMaxDegree Use 20° and 6° on the teaching tank. For a normal setup, enter depression as a positive magnitude, so 6° permits six degrees down. turretDegreesPerSecond, gunDegreesPerSecond Set 18°/s for horizontal traverse and 12°/s for elevation. offset Horizontal offset. Keep 0° when the turret's zero pose already faces forward. ffPointAlignType Selects the aiming alignment reference, the Gun root or the recoiling Dym barrel. Keep the working setup for the first test and compare the resulting muzzle direction. To clear the engine deck or another fixture, add an Override Range for that sector. Symmetric ranges mirror on both sides. Enable asymmetric override ranges for separate sectors, then fill in their start and end azimuths and the elevation and depression available inside each. Aim across the boundary to test how the limits change. The vertical stabilizer has its own speed, elevation and depression limits. The horizontal stabilizer has its own speed and angle. Verify the base limits first. Enable stabilization and compare while moving. In module mode, moduleData.hasOverride can select separate traverse and elevation rates. See the fixed-mount and suspension guide for casemates, hull-assisted traverse and hydraulic suspension. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/MTParameter/maxTurretAngle", "value": "180" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/MTParameter/maxTurretAngle" }, "expect": { "contains": "180" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/MTParameter/UpMaxDegree", "value": "20" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/MTParameter/UpMaxDegree" }, "expect": { "contains": "20" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/MTParameter/DownMaxDegree", "value": "6" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/MTParameter/DownMaxDegree" }, "expect": { "contains": "6" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/MTParameter/turretDegreesPerSecond", "value": "18" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/MTParameter/turretDegreesPerSecond" }, "expect": { "contains": "18" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/MTParameter/gunDegreesPerSecond", "value": "12" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/MTParameter/gunDegreesPerSecond" }, "expect": { "contains": "12" } } ] 3. Test the turret and muzzle Save and rebuild. Stop on level ground and aim at both ends of the travel. A limited turret should stop at its configured bounds. Compare traverse and elevation rates. Use high and low targets to verify the muzzle orientation and elevation limits. Enable stabilization and repeat while turning and driving over rough ground. Fire once and watch the recoil, armor hitboxes and muzzle effect follow their parts. If the turret never moves, check the source hierarchy, effective limits and rates, and the shared asset. If the model rotates while the sight points elsewhere, check pivot axes, horizontal offset and FFPoint. If parts clip, check sector limits and hitbox grouping. Regenerate the prefab after changing the visual hierarchy. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${text}/MTParameter/maxTurretAngle" }, "expect": { "contains": "180" } } ] Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Runtime test pending. Use the entity ID to discover the index of VehicleInitSystem. Read the effective parameters and observe traverse and muzzle direction in the range. manual/en/mod/texture-channel-conversion.title: Pack and unpack ORM textures | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/texture-channel-conversion.summary:
Pack and unpack ORM textures 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run texture-channel-conversion-tools Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "texture": "${fixture}/TutorialORM.png" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } In Substance 3D Designer, connect ambient occlusion, roughness, and metallic to R, G, and B on RGBA Merge. Connect a constant white value to A for an explicit opaque alpha. Adobe RGBA Merge To edit existing ORM, use RGBA Split, then reconnect the channels to RGBA Merge in the required order. Adobe RGBA Split Export a linear data texture and disable sRGB in Unity. See PBR mask channel merging for the Panzer War Mask mapping. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions The Unity sample writes three test values and reads back the PNG. Designer connections follow Adobe's documentation. [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Core.AssetBundleManager/LuaEnv/DoString", "args": [ "local U = CS.UnityEngine
local source = U.Texture2D(2, 2, U.TextureFormat.RGBA32, false, true)
local color = U.Color(0.18, 0.42, 0.72, 1)
for x = 0, 1 do
 for y = 0, 1 do source:SetPixel(x, y, color) end
end
source:Apply()
local png = U.ImageConversion.EncodeToPNG(source)
CS.System.IO.File.WriteAllBytes('${texture}', png)
local copy = U.Texture2D(2, 2, U.TextureFormat.RGBA32, false, true)
assert(U.ImageConversion.LoadImage(copy, png, false))
local pixel = copy:GetPixel(0, 0)
assert(math.abs(color.r - pixel.r) < .005 and math.abs(color.g - pixel.g) < .005)
assert(math.abs(color.b - pixel.b) < .005 and math.abs(color.a - pixel.a) < .005)
U.Object.DestroyImmediate(source)
U.Object.DestroyImmediate(copy)
return "PNG channel sample verified"
", "tutorial-orm", "null" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "PNG channel sample verified" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/ImportAsset", "args": [ "${texture}", "ForceSynchronousImport" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "importer:${texture}/sRGBTexture", "value": "false" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "importer:${texture}/sRGBTexture" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) False" } } ]

manual/en/mod/track-ik-suspension.html.title: Set up a Track IK suspension arm | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/track-ik-suspension.html.summary: Set up a Track IK suspension arm 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run track-ik-suspension --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "model": "${fixture}/Tutorial_TrackIK.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } TrackIK rotates a suspension arm as its road wheel moves. This example uses one arm and one road wheel in the same model prefab. 1. Prepare the model hierarchy Separate the suspension arm into its own node and put its pivot at the hull connection. Add SuspensionArm and RoadWheel under MainBody. Add an empty StandardUCS node in the same prefab and align its up and right axes to the hull. Place the wheel forward of the arm pivot. The example wheel's local position is (0, -0.25, 1). Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${model}", "mode": "create", "component": "UnityEngine.Transform", "children": [ "MainBody/SuspensionArm", "MainBody/RoadWheel", "StandardUCS" ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${model}", "mode": "update", "component": "UnityEngine.Transform", "child": "MainBody/RoadWheel", "values": { "m_LocalPosition": { "x": 0, "y": -0.25, "z": 1 } } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 2. Configure TrackIK Add TrackIK to SuspensionArm. Set Target Wheel to RoadWheel and Standard UCS to StandardUCS. The example uses a Height of 0.1 and a Flip Sign of 1. Leave Use Transform Wrapper enabled. In game, the wrapper at the pivot points its local Z+ toward the target direction while preserving the mesh's initial placement relative to the wrapper. With the wrapper disabled, the script rotates the arm directly, so the arm model's Z+ should point forward along the arm. Repeat on every arm on both sides. In the original KV-2 example, MainBody/TrackIK_011 points to the sixth left road wheel, L6. Its reference is StandardUCS at the model root. Give each arm the wheel that matches its position. The original screenshot used a Height of 0. This tutorial uses 0.1 to illustrate the offset. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${model}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.TrackIK", "child": "MainBody/SuspensionArm", "values": { "isFlip": 1, "height": 0.1, "useTransformWrapper": true }, "references": [ { "property": "target", "child": "MainBody/RoadWheel", "component": "UnityEngine.Transform" }, { "property": "standardUCS", "child": "StandardUCS", "component": "UnityEngine.Transform" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 3. Save and verify Save the collision prefab in Prefab Mode, then recheck both Transform references on each arm. Select an arm in Scene view and check that its guide line points to the intended road wheel. Pack again and check the rotation and height offset in the Vehicle Playground. manual/en/mod/unity-engine-requirements..summary: Unity Editor Version Requirements 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run unity-engine-requirements Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. manual/en/mod/upload-naming-art-standard.title: Art Asset Naming and Upload Standards | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/upload-naming-art-standard.summary:
Art Asset Naming and Upload Standards 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run upload-naming-art-standards Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": {}, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } Keep each contribution to one coherent change, and give assets meaningful names. These rules apply to vehicles, maps, and shared resources in the official asset repository. 1. Branch scope Each branch should contain as few changes as possible — ideally one tank or one aircraft per branch. Do not pile up a large batch of vehicle changes on a single branch and then ask for a merge; such merges will not be accepted. Narrow branches are easier to review one by one, to debug, and to revert. 2. Naming Start every file name with an uppercase letter, for example PantherTurret.fbx rather than pantherTurret.fbx, panther turret.fbx, or the all-caps PANTHERTURRET.FBX. Use a name that says what the asset is, instead of asdf.fbx or NewFile2.fbx. Use the same words for the model, textures, materials, and prefab of one part. Watch your spelling: Turret, not Turet. Check the file names once before exporting. 3. Replacing an FBX when modifying an existing model Export the new FBX from your modelling software and overwrite the FBX at its existing path: either export under the same file name, or copy the new file over the old one in the folder. This cannot be done inside the Unity editor. Keep the existing .meta so Unity continues to identify the FBX by the same GUID. Renaming or rebuilding a child mesh can still change its local file ID. After import, inspect the prefab's mesh references, material slots, and affected hierarchy nodes. Deleting the .meta or importing to a new path creates a new GUID. If you added models inside the FBX, drag the reimported FBX into an empty scene, copy the newly added parts into the original prefab, and save it. Do not add a separate FBX file just because you added one more piece of geometry; otherwise you end up with XXX_fix.fbx, XXX_fix2.fbx, and so on, which turns the project into a mess. 4. Keep normal maps separate from base color maps The normal map and the base color (RGB) map must be two separate textures; do not use one texture for both. In your modelling software, do not feed the RGB map into the Normal input. In Unity, set the normal texture's Texture Type to Normal map, connect the base color texture to the Base Color input, and let each input point at its own texture. The legacy advice "do not set Normal strength" is scoped to imported materials: keep the default Normal strength and do not override it per model without a reason. Unity shaders do expose a Normal strength / Bump scale parameter; the rule is about avoiding arbitrary per-model overrides on imported assets. 5. Avoid duplicate materials Duplicate materials are separate materials that use exactly the same textures. They increase rendering cost and make later bulk edits easy to miss. When duplicating objects in Blender, use Shift+D instead of Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V, and avoid copying objects between files; pasting across files copies the materials with them and creates duplicates. For duplicates that already exist, unify them by hand: replace each object's material reference with the same shared material. The material dropdown lists the candidates, and duplicated ones normally end with .001, .002, and so on; you can also look them up by name in the search box above. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Verify separate base-color and normal texture imports plus stable asset GUID on overwrite. Check an FBX's child mesh references separately. [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Core.AssetBundleManager/LuaEnv/DoString", "args": [ "
local u, e, io = CS.UnityEngine, CS.UnityEditor, CS.System.IO
local base = "${fixture}/TutorialTank_BaseColor.png"
local normal = "${fixture}/TutorialTank_Normal.png"
local tex = u.Texture2D(2, 2, u.TextureFormat.RGBA32, false)
local function write(path, r, g, b)
 for x=0,1 do
 for y=0,1 do
 tex:SetPixel(x, y, u.Color(r,g,b,1))
 end
 end
 tex:Apply()
 io.File.WriteAllBytes(path, u.ImageConversion.EncodeToPNG(tex))
 e.AssetDatabase.ImportAsset(path, e.ImportAssetOptions.ForceSynchronousImport)
end
local ok, issue = pcall(function()
 write(base,0.7,0.6,0.5)
 write(normal,0.5,0.5,1)
 local baseGuid = e.AssetDatabase.AssetPathToGUID(base)
 assert(baseGuid ~= "" and baseGuid ~= e.AssetDatabase.AssetPathToGUID(normal))
 local baseImporter = e.AssetImporter.GetAtPath(base)
 baseImporter.textureType = e.TextureImporterType.Default
 baseImporter.sRGBTexture = true
 baseImporter:SaveAndReimport()
 local normalImporter = e.AssetImporter.GetAtPath(normal)
 normalImporter.textureType = e.TextureImporterType.NormalMap
 normalImporter.sRGBTexture = false
 normalImporter:SaveAndReimport()
 write(base,0.2,0.4,0.6)
 assert(e.AssetDatabase.AssetPathToGUID(base) == baseGuid)
 assert(e.AssetImporter.GetAtPath(base).sRGBTexture)
 assert(e.AssetImporter.GetAtPath(normal).textureType == e.TextureImporterType.NormalMap)
 assert(not e.AssetImporter.GetAtPath(normal).sRGBTexture)
end)
u.Object.DestroyImmediate(tex)
assert(ok,issue)
return "Independent texture imports verified; overwrite kept original asset GUID"
", "art-import-sample", "null" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "overwrite kept original asset GUID" } } ]

manual/en/mod/upload-to-modhub.html.summary: Upload a mod 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run upload-to-modhub Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": {}, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } Send a finished package to ModHub to manage release through the service. Open the upload center In Unity, open Framework → Editor Tools (Ctrl+G). Choose 04. Mod & Build → ModPackage Upload Center. Sign in through the panel's account section. If a Save Account option is offered, use it only on a machine you trust. Select the package Fill in the .modpack file field, or the folder field. A folder is searched recursively for *.modpack files. Build a separate package for each supported Unity build target, such as Windows (StandaloneWindows64), Android, or iOS. Multi-platform builds Updates to an existing mod must keep the same stable GUID and increment the version. Keep the matching .modpack.json sidecar next to every package. Confirm before sending Upload opens a confirmation. Check the signed-in account, package, and version. Cancelling there leaves the package unsent. After confirming, check the server result or package list before retrying. Check the result even if you closed the window. Check the result locally Before uploading, run a local dry run: inspect the archive contents, confirm the platform and version, and verify the sidecar matches. A passing local check is not proof of publication; only the server result and the package list tell you what was accepted. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions The local sample reads the archive, writes its metadata, and checks the Cancel outcome. "asset:${pipeline}/linkedModPackage", "value": "@asset:${package}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" }, "phase": "build" } ] } Start with a Blender model, then build, package, and test-drive a single-turret tracked tank named Tutorial-Tank. The tables give values you can use for a first test. The KV-2 illustrations show the same hierarchy and asset relationships on a finished vehicle. 1. Prepare the project, model, and sounds Follow Project setup to open the SDK project in the required Unity version. Resolve any compilation errors in the Console before opening the mod tools. Check the Console first if a menu is missing. Prepare a visual model and a separate damage model in Blender. You can author base-color and normal textures in tools such as Substance 3D Painter and Photoshop. Gather engine start, idle, and running audio and near and distant firing audio. For the first test, you can reference compatible FMOD configurations already in the SDK. Create a folder for this vehicle in Unity's Project window, with subfolders for models, materials, and the collision prefab. Keep your source files. When re-exporting an existing FBX, keep its path and .meta file to preserve the Unity references. 2. Organize and export the Blender model Keep one root object in Blender's Outliner. Select the child, Shift-select its parent, and use Ctrl+P → Object (Keep Transform). To separate part of a mesh, select its faces in Edit Mode and use P → Selection. Put object origins at their actual pivots so the parts rotate around their own axes in Unity. Node under the model root What to put there MainBody The hull mesh. Turret → Gun → Dym Turret, gun elevation node, and recoiling barrel. Nest all three. Place the turret origin at the turret ring and the gun origin at its elevation pivot. The barrel points forward. LeftWheel and RightWheel Empty grouping objects. Name the road wheels l_1, l_2… and r_1, r_2… and place their origins at the axles. LeftUpperWheel and RightUpperWheel Empty groups for the return rollers. Put each side's rollers in its own group, using names such as lu_1 and ru_1. The current builder orders the wheels by their front-to-back position. LeftTrack and RightTrack Static track meshes or their placeholders. You will set up moving track links and their path later. Model to scale in meters. Select the objects and choose File → Export → FBX. The original guide used Scale 1.00, Apply Scalings → FBX Units Scale, Forward → −Z Forward, and Up → Y Up. In Unity, verify +Z forward and +Y up, then measure the hull against a known dimension. See Correct model axes in Blender. Export a separate, low-poly damage model. Split plates by armor thickness, material type, and moving part. Each plate gets its own thickness in Unity and belongs under the part it moves with. Separate the internal modules too. Follow the damage-model naming conventions. For a small first vehicle, the original art budgets are a useful starting point. Aim for about 20,000 faces or fewer on the visual model, about four materials, textures at 2048 × 2048 or lower, and about 5,000 faces or fewer on the damage model. Cooked Output controls whether the generated prefab goes into the shared Cooked folder or beside the data asset. Check that VehicleInfo resolves to the output. Build, install, and test the mod In the GM Editor, open Mod Build → Create Mod Package. Use a distinct name such as Vehicle-Tutorial-Tank. Open ModPackageBuildPiplineData and drag this vehicle's VehicleInfo into Linked Objects. Verify the associated Linked Mod Package. Use File → Build Settings or Ctrl+Shift+B and switch to the target platform. Verify the active platform, then build the linked resources from the pipeline. In ModPackageData, fill in the name, description, author, and version, then click Package Now. Rebuild the linked objects and package again whenever you change platforms. Find the resulting .modpack under Build/Mod-Package/<platform>/. Check the target and follow Install mods. Use the Windows build for a Windows driving test. Check the build result for the exact file path. In the SDK you can first select VehicleData → Drive (Repack) to open the Vehicle Playground. For an exterior-only test, select Health Based. Select Tutorial Tank and check that it spawns on the ground. Switch to Module Based after you finish the interior. Use the movement controls to drive forward, reverse, and turn both ways. Release them and check that the tank slows. Watch the wheel contact and the direction and fit of the tracks. Aim away from the hull heading and check traverse and elevation. In the range, fire the first shell. It should leave the muzzle, use one round, and reload in about six seconds. Finally, check the hit feedback. If an installed package is missing from the selection list, check Player Pick, the damage mode, and the vehicle types supported by the map. If the tank spawns but will not move, check the torque and TankWheelCollider. If the muzzle moves out of place as you turn the turret, recheck the Gun → Dym hierarchy and firing point from section 7 before repacking. Build the Windows package with the recipe above, then pass its run.json to the test-drive script. python Tools/ManualMcp/TankTutorial/test_drive.py "<build receipt run.json>" Temp/ManualMcp/TankFirstDrive The script uses MCP to install the build, spawn the tank, and verify forward driving, reversing, turning, and a ballistic hit. It switches to Module Based to inspect the loaded modules and checks effect keys in the live object pool. The script exits Play and saves measurements in the output folder. Use the manual drive steps above to check ammo consumption from player input, reload timing, and the appearance of the effects. 11. Try variants after the basic tank works Variant How to extend the basic tank Wheeled vehicle If it still uses the track controller, keep the LeftTrack and RightTrack placeholders. Configure the wheel colliders and review the wheel and track control differences. Slot gun (old M3 Stuart example) Use standard fire, enable Has Slot, and set Slot Count and Slot Duration. The old example used 5 and 3.35. Check the burst and reload timing in the playground. Drum (Progetto 65 example) Set Fire State to Drum. Configure Fire Duration and Reload Times. The old example used 2 seconds and [12.4, 10.3, 8.6, 6.8]. Verify reload at each stage. Magazine (Bat 25t-style example) Choose Advance. In Advance Fire Class, set the short reload, long reload, and rounds per magazine. The old example used 2 seconds, 33 seconds, and 4 rounds. Multiple turrets (BMD-1 and T-35) The BMD-1 example used a secondary weapon for missiles. In the T-35 example, SubTurret01 → SubGun01 → SubDym01 is under the root. The other three secondary turrets use suffixes 02, 03, and 04. Set the turret path from the model root, the gun path from its turret, and the barrel path from its gun. Check muzzle and effect offsets on each. Twin barrels (ST-II) The old hierarchy put SubTurret → SubGun → SubDym under Turret/Gun. Put the second barrel's pivot at its breech. The example used Turret/Gun/SubTurret for the turret path and SubGun and SubDym for the relative paths. Legacy multi-turret setup The old example values illustrate the controls. Tune them for your own mod after testing. For a new multi-turret vehicle, see the current fire-system fields in VehicleTextData. For hull steering, fixed mounts, or hydraulic suspension, see SPG, tank destroyer and Strv setup. If the model is invisible, the gun points the wrong way, or the vehicle is missing after installation, see vehicle development troubleshooting.

manual/en/mod/vehicle-dev-qa.html.title: Troubleshoot a vehicle mod | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/vehicle-dev-qa.html.summary: Troubleshoot a vehicle mod 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run vehicle-dev-qa --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "asset": "${fixture}/Tutorial_VehicleQA.asset" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } A vehicle fails to load Check the installation folder and platform in mod installation. Find the first error in the runtime log and confirm that the package links to the right build pipeline. If the vehicle loads but behaves incorrectly, use VehicleTextData to check vehicle data, hitboxes, tracks, shells, engine sounds and firing sounds. The old project could fail when the package and vehicle shared a name. If the vehicle's internal name is T-72, try naming the package Vehicle-T-72, rebuild, and check whether it loads. If the vehicle appears but fails to run, start from VehicleData and follow its references to the main model, damage prefab, movement data, and firing data. Compare them with a working SDK vehicle. The gun cannot elevate or depress For ordinary guns, use positive magnitudes for Elevate Angle and Depression Angle. For example, UpMaxDegree = 20 and DownMaxDegree = 8 give a range of -8° to 20°. Check the shared turret data and any directional override. maxTurretPositiveAngle and maxTurretNegativeAngle control horizontal traverse. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/Editor/DocumentationSamples/vehicle-text-data/Tutorial_VehicleTextData.asset", "${asset}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/sharedTurretData", "value": "null" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/MTParameter/UpMaxDegree", "value": "20" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/MTParameter/DownMaxDegree", "value": "8" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetTurretParam()/UpMaxDegree" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Single) 20" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetTurretParam()/DownMaxDegree" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Single) 8" } } ] Handling or suspension problems Under VehicleTextData → Mobility, check vehicle mass in kilograms. The original T-72 example used 44100 kg. Check that the field is in kilograms if your source gives mass in tonnes. Open the WheelCollider prefab referenced under Mobility. Its Mass is the wheel's mass. The old example used 320 kg, Radius 0.5, Wheel Damping Rate 0.25, and Suspension Distance 0.2. The old guide suggested keeping wheel mass at or below 1000 kg as a starting point. For Suspension Spring, start with the current template's Spring 205000, Damper 14500, and Target Position 0.5. Tune after testing against the wheel size and vehicle mass. Wheel and friction setup Incorrect shading or missing surfaces Select the normal texture in Unity. Set Texture Type to Normal Map, click Apply, and assign it to the material's normal slot. Turn on Blender's Face Orientation overlay. On a closed mesh, select faces that show red from the outside and use Mesh → Normals → Recalculate Outside in Edit Mode, or flip the selected normals. For intentionally double-sided surfaces, check the material. Use the rendering guide to troubleshoot other visibility problems. A secondary turret reports an index error Check that the error in the log refers to shell data, then open the bulletData list used by each secondary turret. Verify that each list has at least one valid shell and that the selected index is smaller than the list length. Compare against the vehicle modding notes and the template vehicle.
